AUDIT LAYER final assembly (session audit-layer-65, 20 Nov 2026). Usage: python3 -I finalize.py
Reads: full/draft/drafts.json (final merged drafts), the check results of every part in CHECK_ORDER (later results
override earlier ones for the same id), blocks.json, merged/checklist.json (references), merged/checkpoints.json,
merged/sources.json (ONLY the EU / Schedule M source_text of joined items, to find sub-clause boundaries; never WHO /
PIC/S text). Writes: points.json (web-59 contract), owner-review.json, /root/screenshots/audit/audit-layer-owner-review.md,
final-status.json.

Status of an item (point id, or no_point unit id):
  pass    = its latest blind check is PASS (points: all criteria; no_point: PASS and not major) and no code problem
  review  = it was already repaired once (point id contains "-R", or a no_point unit re-listed by a repair) and still
            fails (latest check FAIL or a code problem) -> owner-review list (owner rule: ONE repair only)
  pending = failed / never checked and not yet repaired -> final-status.json lists them; points.json is not final
REF1 (lead): references of a point / other requirement = union of its clause items' references; for a joined item a
reference whose "via" is one of the joined sub-clauses is kept only if a covered unit lies inside that sub-clause's
text span; a reference with via None on a joined item is kept only if ALL duty units of the item are covered by the
same point (hand decisions in ref-hand.json override, each with its reason).

points.question: Is reaching the quality objective treated as the job of senior management, with staff, suppliers and distributors taking part?
points.verify: Verify that the attainment of the quality objective is the responsibility of senior management and has the participation and commitment of staff in different departments and at all levels within the company, the company's suppliers and the distributors.

evidence.what: quality system documents showing who is responsible for the quality objective
senior management and staff on their part in the quality objective

points.question: Is there a pharmaceutical quality system that includes GMP and quality risk management?
points.verify: Verify that, to achieve the quality objective reliably, there is a comprehensively designed and correctly implemented pharmaceutical quality system incorporating Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and Quality Risk Management (QRM).

evidence.what: description of the pharmaceutical quality system
records showing the quality system is implemented

points.question: Has senior management made sure a working quality system exists, has enough resources and has clear roles?
points.verify: Verify that senior management takes the ultimate responsibility to ensure that an effective pharmaceutical quality system is in place, is adequately resourced, and that roles, responsibilities and authorities are defined, communicated and implemented throughout the organisation.

evidence.what: documents defining roles, responsibilities and authorities
records showing these were communicated and implemented
senior management on resourcing of the quality system

points.question: Does senior management lead and actively take part in the quality system so that staff support it?
points.verify: Verify that senior management shows leadership and active participation in the pharmaceutical quality system, and that this ensures the support and commitment of staff at all levels and sites within the organisation to the pharmaceutical quality system.

evidence.what: records showing senior management participation in the quality system
staff at different levels on their commitment to the quality system

points.question: Does the quality system help innovation and continual improvement and tie development closer to manufacturing?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system (which may extend to the pharmaceutical development life-cycle stages) facilitates innovation and continual improvement and strengthens the link between pharmaceutical development and manufacturing activities.

evidence.what: quality system description
records showing improvements and links between development and manufacturing

points.question: Does every part of the quality system have enough resources and upkeep, including people, premises, equipment and facilities?
points.verify: Verify that all parts of the product quality system are adequately resourced and maintained, including being provided with sufficient competent personnel, suitable premises, equipment and facilities.

evidence.what: premises, equipment and facilities provided
records showing personnel numbers and competence

points.question: Do the quality system documents show that the manufacturer takes responsibility for the quality of its products?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer assumes responsibility for the quality of the pharmaceutical products to ensure that they are fit for their intended use, comply with the requirements of the licence and do not place patients at risk due to inadequate safety, quality or efficacy.

evidence.what: quality policy or quality manual stating the manufacturer's responsibility for product quality

points.question: Is the system for making products designed, qualified, planned, run, maintained and continuously improved so that quality is delivered consistently?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that product realisation is achieved by designing, qualifying, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes.

evidence.what: quality system description
records showing the system is implemented, maintained and improved

points.question: Is knowledge about products and processes managed at every lifecycle stage?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that product and process knowledge is managed throughout all lifecycle stages.

evidence.what: procedure or documents on managing product and process knowledge
product and process knowledge records

points.question: Do product design and development consider GMP and the other GXPs?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that pharmaceutical products are designed and developed in a way that takes into account the requirements of GMP and other GXPs such as those of Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) and Good Clinical Practices (GCP).

evidence.what: product design and development documents

points.question: Are production and QC operations clearly written down, with GMP requirements adopted?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that production and quality control operations are clearly specified in a written form and GMP requirements are adopted.

evidence.what: written production and quality control instructions

points.question: Do job descriptions clearly state the responsibilities of managers?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that managerial responsibilities are clearly specified in the job descriptions.

evidence.what: job descriptions

points.question: Are there arrangements for correct starting and packaging materials, supplier selection and monitoring, and checking each delivery?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is the correct material from the approved supply chain.

evidence.what: procedures for materials, supplier selection and monitoring
records showing each delivery was verified

points.question: Are all needed controls on materials, intermediates and bulk, and other in-process controls, calibrations and validations done?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that all necessary controls on starting materials, intermediate products, and bulk products and other in-process controls, calibrations and validations are carried out.

evidence.what: control records for starting materials, intermediate and bulk products
in-process control, calibration and validation records

points.question: Is the finished product processed and checked correctly as the defined procedures say?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that the finished product is correctly processed and checked, according to the defined procedures.

evidence.what: defined procedures for processing and checking finished product
batch processing and checking records

points.question: Is every production batch certified by the authorised persons before it is sold or supplied?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that pharmaceutical products are not sold or supplied before the authorised persons have certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the licence and other applicable regulations relevant to the production, control and release of pharmaceutical products.

evidence.what: batch certification records by authorised persons
sale or supply records

points.question: Are there processes to manage outsourced activities?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that processes are in place to ensure the management of outsourced activities.

evidence.what: procedures for managing outsourced activities
records showing outsourced activities are managed

points.question: Is there a self-inspection or quality audit procedure that regularly assesses the quality system?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that there is a procedure for self-inspection or quality audit that regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the product quality system.

evidence.what: self-inspection or quality audit procedure
self-inspection or quality audit reports

points.question: Are monitoring results for product and processes used in batch release, deviation investigations and preventive action?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that product and processes are monitored and the results taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations and with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future.

evidence.what: product and process monitoring results
batch release, deviation investigation and preventive action records

points.question: Are planned changes evaluated and approved before they are made, considering regulatory notification and approval?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation and approval of planned changes and their approval prior to their implementation, taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required.

evidence.what: arrangements for evaluating and approving planned changes
change records showing evaluation and approval before implementation

points.question: Is each change evaluated after it is made to confirm the aims were met with no unwanted quality effect?
points.verify: Verify that, after implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm that the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended adverse impact on product quality.

evidence.what: evaluations done after implementation of changes

points.question: Are product quality reviews done regularly to check process consistency and find improvement needs?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that regular reviews of the quality of pharmaceutical products are conducted with the objective of verifying the consistency of the process and identifying where there is a need for improvement.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Are quality improvements made that match current process and product knowledge?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge.

evidence.what: records of quality improvements implemented

points.question: Is a quality risk management system in place?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that there is a system for QRM.

evidence.what: QRM system documents
QRM records

points.question: Are deviations, suspected defects and other problems reported, investigated and recorded, with root cause analysis?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that deviations, suspected product defects and other problems are reported, investigated and recorded, and that an appropriate level of root cause analysis is applied during such investigations.

evidence.what: deviation, suspected product defect and problem reports
investigation records showing root cause analysis

points.question: Do investigations name the most likely root causes, lead to corrective and preventive actions, and is their effectiveness followed?
points.verify: Verify that the most likely root causes are identified, that appropriate corrective and preventive actions are identified and taken, and that the effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions is monitored.

evidence.what: investigation records showing root causes
corrective and preventive action records and effectiveness monitoring

points.question: Does senior management take part in periodic reviews of the quality system, held at least yearly?
points.verify: Verify that there are periodic management reviews, with the involvement of senior management, of the operation of the product quality system to identify opportunities for continual improvement of products, processes and the system itself, and that, unless otherwise justified, such reviews are conducted at least annually.

evidence.what: management review records showing dates and senior management involvement
justification where reviews are not at least annual

points.question: Is the quality system defined and written down?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system is defined and documented.

evidence.what: quality system documentation

points.question: Is there a quality manual, or equivalent, that describes the quality management system and management responsibilities?
points.verify: Verify that a quality manual or an equivalent documentation is established and contains a description of the quality management system including management responsibilities.

evidence.what: quality manual or equivalent documentation

points.question: Do effective monitoring and control systems keep process performance and product quality in a state of control?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that a state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.

evidence.what: monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality
process performance and product quality monitoring data

points.question: Does the quality system have satisfactory arrangements so that, as far as possible, products keep their quality in storage, distribution and later handling for their whole shelf-life?
points.verify: Verify that the product quality system appropriate to the manufacture of pharmaceutical products ensures that satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the pharmaceutical products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf-life.

evidence.what: storage, distribution and handling arrangements
storage of pharmaceutical products

points.question: Are quality risk evaluations based on science and process experience, and linked in the end to patient protection?
points.verify: Verify that Quality Risk Management ensures that the evaluation of the risk to quality is based on scientific knowledge, experience with the process and ultimately links to the protection of the patient.

evidence.what: quality risk assessments
QRM procedure

points.question: Does the effort, formality and paperwork of each risk exercise match the risk level?
points.verify: Verify that Quality Risk Management ensures the following: level of effort, formality and documentation of the QRM process is commensurate with the level of risk.

evidence.what: quality risk assessments
QRM procedure

points.question: Are quality reviews done for every product, export-only ones too, to check consistency, specifications, trends and improvements?
points.verify: Verify that regular, periodic or rolling quality reviews of all pharmaceutical products, including products for export only, are conducted with the objective of verifying the consistency of the existing process and the appropriateness of current specifications for both starting materials and finished product, to highlight any trends and to identify product and process improvements.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Are the review results evaluated and a decision made on corrective and preventive actions or revalidation?
points.verify: Verify that the manufacturer evaluates the results of the review and that an assessment is made as to whether corrective and preventive actions or any revalidation shall be undertaken, under the product quality system.

evidence.what: evaluation and assessment in the product quality review reports

points.question: Are the corrective and preventive actions finished on time and effectively, following written procedures?
points.verify: Verify that corrective and preventive actions are completed in a timely and effective manner, according to documented procedures.

evidence.what: documented procedures for corrective and preventive actions
corrective and preventive action records showing completion

points.question: Are there procedures to manage and review these actions, and does self-inspection check that the procedures work?
points.verify: Verify that there are procedures for the on-going management and review of these corrective and preventive actions, and that the effectiveness of these procedures is verified during self-inspection.

evidence.what: procedures for on-going management and review of the actions
self-inspection reports

points.question: Where quality reviews are grouped by product type, is the grouping scientifically justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Where quality reviews are grouped by product type, e.g. solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, or sterile products, verify that this is scientifically justified (recommended).

evidence.what: product quality review reports showing the grouping and its justification

points.question: Is there a technical agreement between the parties that sets out who does what in preparing the quality review?
points.verify: Verify that there is a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the quality review.

evidence.what: technical agreement between the parties

points.question: Does the authorised person for final batch certification make sure the quality review is timely and accurate?
points.verify: Verify that the authorised person responsible for final batch certification ensures that the quality review is performed in a timely manner and is accurate.

evidence.what: product quality review reports showing dates and the authorised person's involvement
authorised person responsible for final batch certification

points.question: Do the quality reviews, normally done and documented every year, cover materials used, critical in-process controls and finished product results?
points.verify: Verify that the quality reviews are normally conducted and documented annually, taking into account previous reviews, and include at least (1) a review of starting materials and packaging materials used for the product, especially those from new sources and in particular the review of supply chain traceability of active substances; and (2) a review of critical in-process controls, and finished product results.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Do the quality reviews, normally done and documented every year, cover failed batches, significant deviations and the resulting corrective and preventive actions?
points.verify: Verify that the quality reviews are normally conducted and documented annually, taking into account previous reviews, and include at least (1) a review of all batches that failed to meet established specifications and their investigation; and (2) a review of all significant deviations or non-conformity, the related investigations and the effectiveness of resultant corrective and preventive actions taken.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Do the quality reviews, normally done and documented every year, cover process and method changes and dossier variations?
points.verify: Verify that the quality reviews are normally conducted and documented annually, taking into account previous reviews, and include at least (1) a review of all changes made to the processes or analytical methods; and (2) a review of dossier variations submitted, granted or refused.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Do the quality reviews, normally done and documented every year, cover stability results and quality related returns, complaints and recalls?
points.verify: Verify that the quality reviews are normally conducted and documented annually, taking into account previous reviews, and include at least (1) a review of the results of the stability monitoring programme and any adverse trends; and (2) a review of all quality related returns, complaints and recalls and the investigations performed at the time.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Do the quality reviews, normally done and documented every year, cover earlier corrective actions and post marketing commitments?
points.verify: Verify that the quality reviews are normally conducted and documented annually, taking into account previous reviews, and include at least (1) a review of adequacy of any other previous corrective actions on product processes or equipment; and (2) post marketing commitments for new dossiers and variations to the dossiers.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Do the quality reviews, normally done and documented every year, cover equipment and utility qualification status, their monitoring results and technical agreements?
points.verify: Verify that the quality reviews are normally conducted and documented annually, taking into account previous reviews, and include at least (1) the qualification status of relevant equipment and utilities, e.g. heating, ventilation and air conditioning, water or compressed gases, and a review of the results of monitoring the output of such equipment and utilities; and (2) a review of technical agreements to ensure that they are up to date.

evidence.what: product quality review reports

points.question: Are all manufacturing processes defined, risk-reviewed and shown able to give product of the required quality every time?
points.verify: Verify that all manufacturing processes are clearly defined, systematically reviewed for associated risks in the light of scientific knowledge and experience and shown to be capable of consistently manufacturing pharmaceutical products of the required quality that comply with their specifications.

evidence.what: manufacturing process definitions
risk reviews of the processes
records showing process capability

points.question: Are qualification and validation carried out?
points.verify: Verify that qualification and validation are performed.

evidence.what: qualification and validation records

points.question: Are there enough people with the right qualifications and training?
points.verify: Verify that all necessary resources are provided, including sufficient and appropriately qualified and trained personnel.

evidence.what: personnel qualification and training records
staffing in the work areas

points.question: Are premises, space, equipment and services adequate and suitable?
points.verify: Verify that all necessary resources are provided, including adequate premises and space and suitable equipment and services.

evidence.what: premises, space, equipment and services

points.question: Are appropriate materials, containers and labels provided?
points.verify: Verify that all necessary resources are provided, including appropriate materials, containers and labels.

evidence.what: materials, containers and labels in use

points.question: Are approved procedures and instructions provided?
points.verify: Verify that all necessary resources are provided, including approved procedures and instructions.

evidence.what: approved procedures and instructions

points.question: Are storage and transport suitable?
points.verify: Verify that all necessary resources are provided, including suitable storage and transport.

evidence.what: storage and transport arrangements

points.question: Are there adequate people, laboratories and equipment for in-process controls?
points.verify: Verify that all necessary resources are provided, including adequate personnel, laboratories and equipment for in-process controls.

evidence.what: personnel, laboratories and equipment used for in-process controls

points.question: Are the legal and official reference books needed for development, manufacturing and QC testing available?
points.verify: Verify that all necessary resources are provided, including books necessary for ensuring compliance with the requirements relating to product development, manufacturing and quality control testing such as the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the Drugs Rules, 1945, the Indian Pharmacopoeia (Current Edition) and other relevant books and guidance documents officially issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.

evidence.what: books and guidance documents available at the plant

points.question: Are instructions and procedures clear, unambiguous and written for the facilities actually provided?
points.verify: Verify that instructions and procedures are written in clear and unambiguous language, specifically applicable to the facilities provided.

evidence.what: instructions and procedures

points.question: Are procedures followed correctly by staff trained to do so?
points.verify: Verify that procedures are carried out correctly and personnel are trained to do so.

evidence.what: procedures being carried out
personnel training records

points.question: Do manufacturing records show that every required step was taken and that quantity and quality were as expected?
points.verify: Verify that records are made (manually or by recording instruments or by both) during manufacture to show that all the steps required by the defined procedures and instructions have in fact been taken and that the quantity and quality of the product are as expected.

evidence.what: batch manufacturing records
records being made during manufacture

points.question: Are significant deviations fully recorded, investigated for root cause and followed by corrective and preventive action?
points.verify: Verify that any significant deviations are fully recorded and investigated with the objective of determining the root cause and that appropriate corrective and preventive action is implemented.

evidence.what: deviation and investigation records
corrective and preventive action records

points.question: Are manufacturing and distribution records kept so that a batch's full history can be traced?
points.verify: Verify that records covering manufacture and distribution, which enable the complete history of a batch to be traced, are retained in a comprehensible and accessible form.

evidence.what: retained manufacturing and distribution records

points.question: Are products stored and distributed properly so that risk to their quality is kept low?
points.verify: Verify that there is proper storage and distribution of the products which minimises any risk to their quality.

evidence.what: product storage
storage and distribution records

points.question: Is there a system to recall any batch from sale or supply?
points.verify: Verify that a system is available to recall any batch of product from sale or supply.

evidence.what: recall system documents

points.question: Are complaints on marketed products examined, defect causes investigated and action taken to stop repeats?
points.verify: Verify that complaints about marketed products are examined, the causes of quality defects investigated and appropriate measures are taken in respect of the defective products to prevent recurrence.

evidence.what: complaint records
quality defect investigation records and measures taken

points.question: Is sanitation and hygiene kept at a high level in all parts of drug manufacture?
points.verify: Verify that a high level of sanitation and hygiene is practiced in every aspect of the manufacture of drugs.

evidence.what: sanitation and hygiene practice during manufacture
sanitation and hygiene records

points.question: Is there one complete sanitation and hygiene programme that removes possible contamination sources?
points.verify: Verify that potential sources of contamination are eliminated through an integrated comprehensive programme of sanitation and hygiene.

evidence.what: sanitation and hygiene programme
potential sources of contamination in manufacture

points.question: Is there a formal change control system for changes that could affect production and control?
points.verify: Verify that a formal change control system is established to evaluate all changes that may affect the production and control of the product.

evidence.what: change control system documents
change control records

points.question: Do written procedures cover how changes are identified, documented, reviewed and approved for all the listed items?
points.verify: Verify that written procedures cover the identification, documentation, appropriate review, and approval of changes in raw materials, specifications, analytical methods, facilities, support systems, equipment (including computer hardware), processing steps, labelling and packaging materials and computer software.

evidence.what: written change procedures

points.question: Are GMP-relevant change proposals drafted, reviewed and approved by the right units and by the quality units?
points.verify: Verify that any proposals for relevant changes to GMP are drafted, reviewed and approved by the appropriate organisational units and reviewed and approved by the quality units.

evidence.what: change proposals showing drafting, review and approval

points.question: Is the possible quality impact of each proposed change evaluated?
points.verify: Verify that the potential impact of the proposed change on the quality of the intermediate or Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) or finished product is evaluated.

evidence.what: impact evaluations in change records

points.question: Is scientific judgement used to decide the extra testing and validation needed for a change to a validated process?
points.verify: Verify that scientific judgement is used to determine what additional testing and validation studies are appropriate to justify a change in a validated process.

evidence.what: change records showing how additional testing and validation studies were decided

points.question: When approved changes are made, are all affected documents revised?
points.verify: Verify that, when implementing the approved changes, measures are taken to ensure that all the documents affected by the changes are revised.

evidence.what: change records listing affected documents
revised documents

points.question: Is the first batch made or tested after a change evaluated?
points.verify: Verify that, after the change has been implemented, there is an evaluation of the first batch produced or tested under the change.

evidence.what: evaluation of the first batch produced or tested under the change

points.question: Is it evaluated whether critical changes could affect retest or expiry dates?
points.verify: Verify that the potential for critical changes to affect established retest or expiry dates is evaluated.

evidence.what: change records showing evaluation of effect on retest or expiry dates

points.question: Is the self-inspection programme built to find GMP gaps and to propose corrective actions?
points.verify: Verify that the self-inspection programme is designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions.

evidence.what: self-inspection programme

points.question: Do records show that self-inspections are done on a routine basis?
points.verify: Verify that self-inspections are performed routinely. They may, in addition, be performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced.

evidence.what: records of self-inspections performed

points.question: Are the people on the self-inspection team able to judge GMP implementation objectively?
points.verify: Verify that the team responsible for self-inspection consists of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively.

evidence.what: list of self-inspection team members
team members, on their objectivity

points.question: Do records show that every corrective action recommended by self-inspection was carried out?
points.verify: Verify that all recommendations for corrective action have been implemented.

evidence.what: self-inspection recommendations for corrective action
records showing their implementation

points.question: Is there a written self-inspection procedure, and is an effective follow-up programme in place?
points.verify: Verify that the procedure for self-inspection is documented and that there is an effective follow-up programme.

evidence.what: self-inspection procedure
follow-up programme
follow-up records

points.question: Are there written self-inspection instructions that set a minimum and uniform standard?
points.verify: Verify that written instructions for self-inspection are established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.

evidence.what: written instructions for self-inspection

points.question: Has management appointed a self-inspection team of GMP-familiar experts in their own fields?
points.verify: Verify that management has appointed a self-inspection team consisting of experts in their respective fields who are familiar with GMP.

evidence.what: management appointment of the self-inspection team
records showing members' field expertise and GMP familiarity

points.question: Do records show a self-inspection at least once every year?
points.verify: Verify that self-inspections are conducted at least once in a year; the frequency may depend on company requirements but not be less than this.

evidence.what: self-inspection reports with dates

points.question: Does the self-inspection procedure state how often self-inspections are done?
points.verify: Verify that the frequency of self-inspection is stated in the procedure.

evidence.what: self-inspection procedure

points.question: Is a report written when each self-inspection is finished, and does it have all the required contents?
points.verify: Verify that a report is made at the completion of a self-inspection and that the report includes (a) self-inspection results; (b) evaluation and conclusions; and (c) recommended corrective actions.

evidence.what: self-inspection reports

points.question: Where the self-inspection instructions include GMP questionnaires, do these cover at least all the listed items (recommended)?
points.verify: Where the written instructions for self-inspection include questionnaires on good manufacturing practices requirements, verify that these are covering at least the following items, namely: (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) quality control (QC); (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; and (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken (recommended).

evidence.what: written instructions for self-inspection, including questionnaires

points.question: Is an effective programme in place to follow up after self-inspections?
points.verify: Verify that there is an effective follow-up programme.

evidence.what: follow-up programme
follow-up records

points.question: Do records show that company management reviews the self-inspection report and the corrective actions?
points.verify: Verify that the company management evaluates both the self-inspection report and the corrective actions as necessary.

evidence.what: records of management evaluation of the report and corrective actions

points.question: Have risk assessments been done to find the possible hazards to operators and to the environment?
points.verify: Verify that risk assessments have been carried out for products containing hazardous substances to determine the potential hazards to operators and to the environment.

evidence.what: risk assessments for products containing hazardous substances

points.question: Does the risk assessment identify the phases of production and control that come under these guidelines?
points.verify: Verify that the risk assessment also determines which phase of the product production and control cycles, from manufacture of the API to distribution of the finished product, would fall under the requirements of these guidelines.

evidence.what: risk assessment

points.question: Do the environmental risk assessments cover both contamination through air and through liquid effluent?
points.verify: Verify that risk assessments applicable to the environment include airborne contamination as well as liquid effluent contamination.

evidence.what: risk assessments applicable to the environment

points.question: Where the risk assessment shows a risk to people or the environment, do the facility's design and operation follow this Schedule?
points.verify: Verify that, where the risk assessment determines that the products or materials being handled pose a risk to the operators or to the public or to the environment, the guidelines followed for the design and operation of the facility are as detailed in this Schedule.

evidence.what: risk assessment conclusions
guidelines followed for facility design and operation

points.question: Does the risk assessment use the available toxicological data and the workplace health and safety requirements for OELs?
points.verify: Verify that the toxicological data available, such as permissible occupational exposure levels (OEL) for the product, are taken into account when conducting the risk assessment, and that the risk assessment takes into account occupational health and safety requirements for OELs in the work environment.

evidence.what: risk assessment

points.question: Do the plant's biosafety arrangements follow the Central Government's guidelines on this subject?
points.verify: Verify that biosafety considerations follow the guidelines issued by the Central Government in this regard.

evidence.what: procedure or records showing biosafety considerations
Central Government biosafety guidelines

points.question: Do manufacturing records agree with the other specifications set in the clinical trial approvals, marketing authorisation or product summary files?
points.verify: Verify that manufacturing is consistent with other specifications set out in the product summary files, marketing authorisation or clinical trial approvals, for example the number of generations (expressed as doublings or passages) between the seed lot or cell bank and the finished product.

evidence.what: product summary files, marketing authorisation or clinical trial approvals
manufacturing records

points.question: Do records show that virus removal or inactivation and other specific and critical steps of manufacture were validated?
