points.verify: Verify that, regardless of how many sites are involved, the QP performing certification of the finished product ensures that all necessary steps have been completed under accepted pharmaceutical quality systems to assure compliance of the batch with GMP, the MA and any other legal obligations in the Member State where certification is taking place.

evidence.what: records the QP relies on for certification
certifying QP

points.question: Does every EU site that carries out manufacturing steps have a QP?
points.verify: Verify that, for manufacturing steps performed at sites in the EU, each manufacturing site has at least one QP.

evidence.what: document or records showing the QP(s) of each site

points.question: Where a site does only part of the manufacture of a batch, does a QP of that site confirm its operations?
points.verify: Verify that, where the site only undertakes partial manufacturing operations in relation to a batch, a QP at that site at least confirms that the operations undertaken by the site have been performed in accordance with GMP and the terms of the written agreement detailing the operations for which the site is responsible.

evidence.what: QP confirmations for the batch
written agreement on the site's operations

points.question: Where the QP confirms that those operations comply with the MA, can the QP get the MA details needed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, if the QP is responsible for providing confirmation of compliance for those operations with the relevant MA, the QP has access to the necessary details of the MA (recommended).

evidence.what: MA details available to the QP
QP, on access to MA details

points.question: Is any split of batch compliance responsibilities between QPs written in a document that all parties formally agreed?
points.verify: Verify that any sharing of responsibilities amongst QPs in relation to compliance of a batch is defined in a document formally agreed by all parties.

evidence.what: agreed document on shared QP responsibilities

points.question: Does the document on shared QP responsibilities say who assesses the effect of deviations on the batch (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that this document details responsibility for assessment of the impact any deviation(s) has/have on compliance of the batch with GMP and the MA (recommended).

evidence.what: agreed document on shared QP responsibilities

points.question: Does the QP look at storage and transport conditions before certifying a batch (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that conditions of storage and transport for the batch and the sample, if sent separately, are taken into account by the QP before certification of a batch (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing storage and transport conditions considered by the QP
certifying QP

points.question: Does the certifying QP make sure every finished batch was made in line with GMP and the marketing authorisation?
points.verify: Verify that the QP certifying the finished product ensures that each finished medicinal product batch has been manufactured in accordance with GMP and the MA.

evidence.what: records the QP relies on for certification
certifying QP

points.question: Where no MRA or similar agreement exists with the exporting country, do records show the batch was fully tested in a Member State?
points.verify: Verify that, unless an MRA or similar agreement is in place between the EU and the exporting country, the QP also ensures that the finished medicinal product batch has undergone in a Member State a full qualitative analysis, a quantitative analysis of at least all the active substances and all the other tests or checks necessary to ensure the quality of medicinal products is in accordance with the requirements of the MA.

evidence.what: test results of the batch from a Member State
MRA or similar agreement, if any

points.question: Do samples of imported product fully represent the batch (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that sampling of imported product is fully representative of the batch (recommended).

evidence.what: sampling procedure for imported product
sampling records

points.question: Where samples are taken at the third country manufacturing site, is this done under a documented, technically justified approach (recommended)?
points.verify: Where samples are taken at the manufacturing site in the third country instead of after arrival in the EU, verify that this is done in accordance with a technically justified approach which is documented within the company's quality system (recommended).

evidence.what: documented technical justification in the quality system

points.question: Does a written agreement between the sites set out who is responsible for sampling (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that responsibilities in relation to the sampling are defined in a written agreement between the sites (recommended).

evidence.what: written agreement between the sites

points.question: Do samples taken outside the EU travel under transport conditions equal to those of their batch (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any samples taken outside the EU are shipped under equivalent transport conditions as the batch that they represent (recommended).

evidence.what: transport condition records of samples and batch

points.question: Where sampling is done at a third country manufacturing site, does the technical justification contain a formal risk management process (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where sampling is performed at a third country manufacturing site, the technical justification includes a formal Quality Risk Management process to identify and manage any risks associated with this approach (recommended).

evidence.what: technical justification with Quality Risk Management process

points.question: Is the risk management process for third country sampling fully documented, and does it cover an audit and a transport evaluation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that this is fully documented and includes at least an audit of the manufacturing activity including any sampling activity at the third country site and an evaluation of subsequent transportation steps of both the batch and samples to ensure that the samples are representative of the imported batch (recommended).

evidence.what: documented Quality Risk Management process
audit report and transport evaluation

points.question: Is the risk management process fully documented, and does it hold a full scientific study with supporting data (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that this is fully documented and includes at least a comprehensive scientific study, including data to support any conclusions that samples taken in the third country are representative of the batch after importation (recommended).

evidence.what: documented Quality Risk Management process
scientific study with its data

points.question: Does the study describe the third country sampling process and the transport conditions, with any differences justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that this study at least includes a description of the sampling process in the third country and a description of the transported conditions of the sample and the imported batch, and that any differences are justified (recommended).

evidence.what: scientific study

points.question: Does the study compare third country samples with post-import samples and deal with the time gap before importation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that this study at least includes a comparative analysis of samples taken in the third country and samples taken after importation, and consideration of the time interval between sampling and importation of the batch and generation of data to support appropriate defined limits (recommended).

evidence.what: scientific study with comparative data

points.question: Is the risk management process fully documented, and does it provide for random periodic testing of post-import samples (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that this is fully documented and includes at least provision for random periodic analysis of samples taken after importation to justify ongoing reliance on samples taken in a third country (recommended).

evidence.what: documented Quality Risk Management process

points.question: Are unexpected or confirmed out of specification results reviewed, reported to the Supervisory Authority and investigated as possible quality defects (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that this is fully documented and includes at least a review of any unexpected result or confirmed out of specification result; that these results, which may have implications for reliance on sampling performed at the third country manufacturing site, are notified to the Supervisory Authority for the site where certification is performed; and that such an occurrence is regarded as a potential quality defect and investigated in line with the guidance in Chapter 8 of EudraLex, Volume 4, Part I (recommended).

evidence.what: documented Quality Risk Management process
notifications to the Supervisory Authority
investigation records

points.question: Where QPs rely on the testing of the first imported finished batch to certify other batches, is there a documented risk-based justification (recommended)?
points.verify: Where the QPs certifying the different finished product batches base their decision on the quality control testing of the first imported finished batch, verify that a justification has been documented based on Quality Risk Management principles, and that it takes into account the provisions of paragraph 1.5.6 in relation to reliance on any samples taken in third countries (recommended).

evidence.what: documented justification

points.question: Is there documented proof that the bulk storage and the finished batch storage and transport conditions were met (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that evidence is available to ensure that the integrity and identity of the imported finished product batch has been established through documented verification of at least the following: relevant requirements for storage of the bulk product prior to packaging have been satisfied; and the finished product batch has been stored and transported under the needed conditions (recommended).

evidence.what: documented verification of bulk storage
documented verification of batch storage and transport

points.question: Is there documented proof of consignment security, correct product identification and representative samples for the imported batch (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that evidence is available to ensure that the integrity and identity of the imported finished product batch has been established through documented verification of at least the following: the consignment has remained secure and there is no evidence of tampering during storage or transportation; correct identification of the product has been established; and the sample(s) tested are representative of all finished product batches derived from the bulk batch (recommended).

evidence.what: documented verification of consignment security and product identification
documented verification that samples are representative

points.question: Does the QP personally make sure, before certifying, that the MIA allows it, national duties are met and certification is entered in a register?
points.verify: Verify that the QP personally ensures that the following operational responsibilities are fulfilled prior to certification of a batch for release to market or for export: certification is permitted under the terms of the MIA; any additional duties and requirements of national legislation are complied with; and certification is recorded in a register or equivalent document.

evidence.what: MIA
certification register or equivalent document
QP

points.question: Does the QP have continuing assurance that relying on the pharmaceutical quality system is justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, as the QP will need to rely on the pharmaceutical quality system, the QP has on-going assurance that this reliance is well founded (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the QP's on-going assurance
QP

points.question: Does the QP make sure that all manufacturing and testing work for the product followed GMP?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that all activities associated with manufacture and testing of the medicinal product have been conducted in accordance with the principles and guidelines of GMP.

evidence.what: records the QP relies on for certification
QP

points.question: Is the full supply chain up to certification written down and at hand for the QP?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the entire supply chain of the active substance and medicinal product up to the stage of certification is documented and available for the QP.

evidence.what: supply chain document

points.question: Does the supply chain document cover the material manufacturing sites, and is it preferably a full diagram showing each party (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the supply chain document includes the manufacturing sites of the starting materials and packaging materials for the medicinal product and any other materials deemed critical through a risk assessment of the manufacturing process, and that it is preferably in the format of a comprehensive diagram where each party, including subcontractors of critical steps such as the sterilisation of components and equipment for aseptic processing, are included (recommended).

evidence.what: supply chain document or diagram

points.question: Have all audits of the product's manufacturing, testing and active substance sites been done, and can the certifying QP see the reports?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that all audits of sites involved in the manufacture and the testing of the medicinal products and in the manufacture of the active substance have been carried out and that the audit reports are available to the QP performing the certification.

evidence.what: audit reports of the sites

points.question: Do the manufacturing, analysis and certification sites all match the marketing authorisation for the intended territory?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that all sites of manufacture, analysis and certification are compliant with the terms of the MA for the intended territory.

evidence.what: MA for the intended territory
records showing the sites used

points.question: Do the manufacturing and testing activities match what the marketing authorisation describes?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that all manufacturing activities and testing activities are consistent with those described in the MA.

evidence.what: MA
manufacturing and testing records

points.question: Do the source and specifications of the materials used in the batch match the marketing authorisation?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the source and specifications of starting materials and packaging materials used in the batch are compliant with the MA.

evidence.what: MA
material specifications
records showing the source of materials used in the batch

points.question: Are supplier quality management systems in place so that only materials of the right quality are supplied?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that supplier quality management systems are in place that ensure only materials of the required quality have been supplied.

evidence.what: supplier quality management procedure
supplier quality management records

points.question: Do records show the active substances were made under GMP and, where it applies, distributed under GDP?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that, for medicinal products that fall within the scope of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended, or Directive 2001/82/EC, the active substances have been manufactured in accordance with GMP and, where required, distributed in accordance with Good Distribution Practice (GDP) for Active Substances.

evidence.what: records showing GMP manufacture and GDP distribution of active substances

points.question: Does the import of active substances for human medicines meet the Directive's import rules (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the importation of active substances used in the manufacture of medicinal products for human use complies with the requirements of Article 46(b) of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended (recommended).

evidence.what: records of active substance importation

points.question: Do records show the excipients were made under the GMP ascertained for them?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that, for medicinal products that fall within the scope of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended, the excipients have been manufactured in accordance with the ascertained GMP referred to in Article 46 (f) of that Directive.

evidence.what: records showing the ascertained GMP for excipients

points.question: When relevant, does the TSE status of every material used in the batch match the marketing authorisation?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that, when relevant, the TSE (Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathy) status of all materials used in batch manufacture is compliant with the terms of the MA.

evidence.what: records showing TSE status of materials
MA

points.question: Are the records complete and endorsed, and do they show every in-process control and check was done?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that all records are complete and endorsed by appropriate personnel, and that all required in-process controls and checks have been made.

evidence.what: batch records
in-process control and check records

points.question: Are the manufacturing and testing processes still in their validated state?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that all manufacturing and testing processes remain in the validated state.

evidence.what: records showing the validated state of processes

points.question: Are the staff trained and qualified as appropriate?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that personnel are trained and qualified as appropriate.

evidence.what: personnel training and qualification records

points.question: Do the finished product QC results meet the specification in the marketing authorisation or the authorised real time release programme?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that finished product quality control (QC) test data complies with the Finished Product Specification described in the MA, or where authorised, the Real Time Release Testing programme.

evidence.what: finished product QC test data
Finished Product Specification in the MA
Real Time Release Testing programme, where authorised

points.question: Have post-marketing commitments to regulators on manufacture or testing been dealt with?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that any regulatory post-marketing commitments relating to manufacture or testing of the product have been addressed.

evidence.what: records showing post-marketing commitments addressed

points.question: Do the on-going stability results still back certification?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that on-going stability data continues to support certification.

evidence.what: on-going stability data

points.question: Has the effect of every manufacturing or testing change been assessed and any extra checks and tests finished?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the impact of any change to product manufacturing or testing has been evaluated and any additional checks and tests are complete.

evidence.what: change impact evaluations
results of additional checks and tests

points.question: Are all investigations on the batch, OOS and OOT included, far enough along to support certification?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that all investigations pertaining to the batch being certified (including out of specification and out of trend investigations) have been completed to a sufficient level to support certification.

evidence.what: investigation records for the batch

points.question: Has it been checked that open complaints, investigations or recalls do not stop this batch from being certified?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that any on-going complaints, investigations or recalls do not negate the conditions for certification of the batch in question.

evidence.what: on-going complaint, investigation and recall records
QP

points.question: Are the technical agreements that are needed in place?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the required technical agreements are in place.

evidence.what: technical agreements

points.question: Is the self-inspection programme running and up to date?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the self-inspection programme is active and current.

evidence.what: self-inspection programme
self-inspection records

points.question: Are suitable distribution and shipment arrangements in place?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that the appropriate arrangements for distribution and shipment are in place.

evidence.what: distribution and shipment arrangements

points.question: For human medicines meant for the Union market, are the safety features on the packaging where appropriate?
points.verify: Verify that the QP ensures that, in the case of medicinal products for human use intended to be placed on the market in the Union, the safety features referred to in Article 54(o) of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended, have been affixed to the packaging, where appropriate.

evidence.what: packaging records showing safety features
safety features on packs

points.question: For parallel import or parallel distribution, is there authority approval for repackaging of an already released batch?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of parallel importation and parallel distribution, any repackaging operation carried out on a batch which has already been released is approved by the competent authority of the intended market.

evidence.what: competent authority approval for repackaging

points.question: Before certifying a repacked batch, does the QP confirm the parallel importation and parallel distribution rules are met (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, prior to certification of a repacked batch, the QP confirms compliance with national requirements for parallel importation and EU rules for parallel distribution (recommended).

evidence.what: QP confirmation for the repacked batch

points.question: Does the QP named in the marketing authorisation of the repackaged product certify how the repackaging was done?
points.verify: Verify that the QP of the MIA holder, who is named responsible for the certification of the batch in the MA of the repackaged finished product, certifies that the repackaging has been performed in accordance with the relevant authorisation pertaining to the repackaged product and GMP.

evidence.what: certification of the repackaged batch
MA of the repackaged finished product

points.question: Does the QP enter each certification in a register or similar document kept for this?
points.verify: Verify that the certification of a medicinal product is recorded by the QP in a register or equivalent document provided for that purpose.

evidence.what: certification register or equivalent document

points.question: Does the certification record show that each production batch meets the Directive provisions (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the record shows that each production batch satisfies the provisions of Article 51 of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended, or Article 55 of Directive 2001/82/EC (recommended).

evidence.what: certification register or equivalent document

points.question: Is the certification record kept current and held ready for the authority for the set period, five years at least?
points.verify: Verify that the record is kept up to date as operations are carried out and remains at the disposal of the agents of the competent authority for the period specified in the provisions of the Member State concerned and in any event for at least five years.

evidence.what: certification register or equivalent document

points.question: Is the control report or other proof of release provided for a batch going to another Member State (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the control report referred to in Article 51 of Directive 2001/83/EC, as amended, or Article 55 of Directive 2001/82/EC or another proof for release to the market in question, based on an equivalent system, is made available for the batch in order to be exempted from further controls when entering another Member State (recommended).

evidence.what: control report or other proof of release for the batch

points.question: Where a QP confirms or certifies a batch after an unexpected deviation, were all registered specifications met (recommended)?
points.verify: Where a QP confirms compliance or certifies a batch where an unexpected deviation concerning the manufacturing process and/or the analytical control methods from details contained within the MA and/or GMP has occurred, verify that registered specifications for active substances, excipients, packaging materials and medicinal products are met (recommended).

evidence.what: deviation record for the batch
test results against registered specifications

points.question: Do records show a thorough investigation of the deviation and correction of its root cause (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the deviation is thoroughly investigated and the root cause corrected (recommended).

evidence.what: deviation investigation records
records showing the root cause corrected

points.question: Is the effect of the deviation assessed through a quality risk management process (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the impact of the deviation is assessed in accordance with a quality risk management process using an appropriate approach such as described in Part III of the GMP Guide (recommended).

evidence.what: risk assessment of the deviation

points.question: Does the risk assessment of the deviation cover batch impact, stability follow-up and, for biologicals, unexpected effects (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the quality risk management process includes: evaluation of the potential impact of the deviation on quality, safety or efficacy of the batch(es) concerned and conclusion that the impact is negligible; consideration of the need to include the affected batch(es) in the ongoing stability programme; and, in the case of biological medicinal products, consideration that any deviations from the approved process can have an unexpected impact on safety and efficacy (recommended).

evidence.what: risk assessment of the deviation

points.question: Does the certifying QP know of and weigh deviations that could affect GMP or marketing authorisation compliance, also when several QPs share the work (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, taking account that responsibilities may be shared between more than one QPs involved in the manufacture and control of a batch, the QP performing certification of a batch of medicinal product is aware of and takes into consideration any deviations which have the potential to impact compliance with GMP and/or compliance with the MA (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing deviations considered by the certifying QP
certifying QP

points.question: Where dealing with an unexpected deviation calls for a variation to the marketing authorisation to keep making the product, has the variation been submitted (recommended)?
points.verify: Where the investigation of an unexpected deviation and the correction of its root cause make a variation to the MA necessary for the continued manufacture of the product, verify that the variation is submitted (recommended).

evidence.what: deviation records showing whether a variation to the MA is needed
variation submission to the MA

points.question: Do records show that batches go out for sale or supply only once a QP has certified them (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that batches of medicinal products are only released for sale or supply to the market after certification by a QP as described above (recommended).

evidence.what: batch certification records
batch release records

points.question: Does an uncertified batch stay at the manufacturing site or move only under quarantine to an authority-approved site (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, until a batch is certified, it remains at the site of manufacture or is shipped under quarantine to another site which has been approved for that purpose by the relevant Competent Authority (recommended).

evidence.what: shipment records of uncertified batches
Competent Authority approval of the receiving site
uncertified batches held at the site

points.question: Are there safeguards that stop uncertified batches from reaching saleable stock (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that safeguards to ensure that uncertified batches are not transferred to saleable stock are in place; they may be physical in nature, e.g. the use of segregation and labelling, or electronic in nature, e.g. the use of validated computerised systems (recommended).

evidence.what: safeguards on uncertified batches
procedure describing the safeguards

points.question: Do the safeguards against early release stay in force when uncertified batches move between authorised sites (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when uncertified batches are moved from one authorised site to another, the safeguards to prevent premature release remain (recommended).

evidence.what: transfer records of uncertified batches
safeguards on transferred batches

points.question: Does a technical agreement set out how the stock site is told about QP certification (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the steps necessary to notify QP certification to the site where the transfer to saleable stock is to take place are defined within a technical agreement (recommended).

evidence.what: technical agreement

points.question: Is the QP's notice of certification to the site formal, clear and handled under the documentation chapter (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that such notification by a QP to the site is formal and unambiguous and is subject to the requirements of Chapter 4 of EudraLex, Volume 4, Part I (recommended).

evidence.what: QP notifications of certification

points.question: Does the confirmation of partial manufacturing identify the manufacturer, the product and stage, the batch and the site?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation of partial manufacturing carries the letter head of the manufacturer who carried out the manufacturing activity and gives the name of the product and a description of the manufacturing stage (e.g. paracetamol 500 mg tablets, primary packaging into blister packs), the batch number, and the name and address of the site carrying out the partial manufacturing.

evidence.what: confirmations of partial manufacturing

points.question: Does the confirmation of partial manufacturing refer to the Technical Quality Agreement?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation of partial manufacturing contains a reference to the Technical Quality Agreement (in accordance with Chapter 7 of the Guide).

evidence.what: confirmations of partial manufacturing

points.question: Does the confirmation of partial manufacturing contain the full confirmation statement on GMP and agreement compliance?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation of partial manufacturing contains a confirmation statement saying that the manufacturing stages referred to in the Technical Quality Agreement have been carried out in full compliance with the GMP requirements of the EU and the terms described in the Agreement for ensuring compliance with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation(s) as provided by the Contract Giver/manufacturer certifying and releasing the batch.

evidence.what: confirmations of partial manufacturing

points.question: Is the confirmation of partial manufacturing named, signed and dated by the Qualified Person?
points.verify: Verify that the confirmation of partial manufacturing shows the name of the Qualified Person confirming the partial manufacturing, the signature of the Qualified Person confirming the partial manufacturing, and the date of signature.

evidence.what: confirmations of partial manufacturing

points.question: Does the batch certificate identify the releasing manufacturer, the product, the batch and the destination?
points.verify: Verify that the batch certificate carries the letter head of the batch certifying and releasing manufacturer and gives the name, strength/potency, dosage form and package size (identical to the text on the finished product package), the batch number of the finished product, and the name of the destination country/countries of the batch, at least when within the EU.

evidence.what: batch certificates
text on the finished product package

points.question: Does the batch certificate contain the full certification statement on GMP and marketing authorisation compliance?
points.verify: Verify that the batch certificate contains a certification statement saying that all the manufacturing stages of this batch of finished product have been carried out in full compliance with the GMP requirements of the EU and, when within the EU, with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation(s) of the destination country/countries.

evidence.what: batch certificates

points.question: Is the batch certificate named, signed and dated by the Qualified Person?
points.verify: Verify that the batch certificate shows the name of the Qualified Person certifying the batch, the signature of the Qualified Person certifying the batch, and the date of signature.

evidence.what: batch certificates

points.question: Where process information is used instead of end-product testing for batch release, is this authorised and based on product and process knowledge (recommended)?
points.verify: Where information collected during the manufacturing process is used instead of end-product testing for batch release, verify that this is in specific circumstances, authorised, and based on product knowledge and process understanding (recommended).

evidence.what: authorisation for this form of batch release
batch release records

points.question: Are the separate activities needed for this form of batch release built into the quality system (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any separate activities needed for this form of batch release are integrated into the Pharmaceutical Quality System (PQS) (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering this form of batch release

points.question: Do records show contact with the regulatory authorities before and during the assessment that leads to RTRT approval?
points.verify: Verify that there was interaction with all relevant regulatory authorities prior and during the assessment process preceding regulatory approval.

evidence.what: records of interaction with regulatory authorities

points.question: Does the RTRT design show that real time measurement and control predict the finished product attributes accurately (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when designing the RTRT strategy, the following minimum criterion is established and met: real time measurement and control of relevant in-process material attributes and process parameters are accurate predictors of the corresponding finished product attributes (recommended).

data showing the prediction of finished product attributes

points.question: Is the combination of attributes and controls that replaces finished product attributes backed by scientific evidence (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when designing the RTRT strategy, the following minimum criterion is established and met: the valid combination of relevant assessed material attributes and process controls to replace finished product attributes is established with scientific evidence based on material, product and process knowledge (recommended).

evidence.what: RTRT strategy
scientific evidence for the combination

points.question: Do the process measurements and other in-process test data give a robust basis for RTRT and batch release (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when designing the RTRT strategy, the following minimum criterion is established and met: the combined process measurements (process parameters and material attributes) and any other test data generated during the manufacturing process provide a robust foundation for RTRT and the batch release decision (recommended).

evidence.what: RTRT strategy
process measurements and test data from manufacturing

points.question: Is the RTRT strategy built into the quality system and controlled through it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the RTRT strategy is integrated and controlled through the PQS (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering the RTRT strategy

points.question: Does the RTRT strategy in the quality system cover risk management, change control and the control strategy (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the RTRT strategy in the PQS includes or references information at least of: quality risk management, including a full process related risk assessment, in accordance with the principles described in EudraLex, Volume 4, Part I Chapter 1 and Part II Chapter 2; the change control program; and the control strategy (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering the RTRT strategy

points.question: Does the RTRT strategy in the quality system cover training, qualification and validation, and deviations/CAPA (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the RTRT strategy in the PQS includes or references information at least of: the specific personnel training program; the qualification and validation policy; and the deviation/CAPA system (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering the RTRT strategy

points.question: Does the RTRT strategy in the quality system cover sensor or equipment failure and periodic review of the RTRT plan (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the RTRT strategy in the PQS includes or references information at least of: a contingency procedure in case of a process sensor/equipment failure; and a periodic review/assessment program to measure the effectiveness of the RTRT plan for continued assurance of product quality (recommended).

evidence.what: PQS documents covering the RTRT strategy

points.question: Do change records show a risk and reproducibility assessment, a risk-based justification and full documentation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any change that could potentially impact product manufacturing and testing, or the validated status of facilities, systems, equipment, analytical methods or processes, is assessed for risk to product quality and impact on reproducibility of the manufacturing process (recommended). points.question: Is each change evaluated after it is implemented to show no harm to product quality (recommended)?

points.verify: Verify that products returned from the market and which have left the control of the manufacturer are destroyed unless without doubt their quality is satisfactory, and that they are considered for re-sale, re-labelling or recovery in a subsequent batch only after they have been critically assessed by the Quality Control Department in accordance with a written procedure (recommended).

evidence.what: written procedure for assessment of returned products
Quality Control assessment records of returned products
records of returned products and their disposition

points.question: Does the assessment of returned products look at the product's nature, storage needs, condition, history and time since issue (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the nature of the product, any special storage conditions it requires, its condition and history, and the time elapsed since it was issued are all taken into account in the assessment of returned products (recommended).

evidence.what: assessment records of returned products

points.question: Where there is any doubt about a returned product's quality, is it kept out of re-issue and re-use (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where any doubt arises over the quality of the returned product, it is not considered suitable for re-issue or re-use, although basic chemical reprocessing to recover active ingredient may be possible (recommended).

evidence.what: assessment and disposition records of returned products

points.question: Is every action taken on returned products properly recorded (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any action taken on returned products is appropriately recorded (recommended).

evidence.what: records of action taken on returned products

points.question: Is there a system with suitable procedures to record, assess, investigate and review complaints and, if needed, to recall products from distribution (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in order to protect public and animal health, a system and appropriate procedures are in place to record, assess, investigate and review complaints including potential quality defects, and if necessary, to effectively and promptly recall medicinal products for human or veterinary use and investigational medicinal products from the distribution network (recommended).

evidence.what: complaint and quality defect procedures
recall procedures

points.question: Is Quality Risk Management used when quality defects are investigated and assessed and when recall and other risk-reducing decisions are made (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that Quality Risk Management principles are applied to the investigation and assessment of quality defects and to the decision-making process in relation to product recalls corrective and preventative actions and other risk-reducing actions (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation and assessment records
records of decisions on recalls, corrective and preventative actions and other risk-reducing actions

points.question: Are all concerned competent authorities told in good time of a confirmed quality defect that may lead to a recall or an abnormal supply restriction (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all concerned competent authorities are informed in a timely manner in case of a confirmed quality defect (faulty manufacture, product deterioration, detection of falsification, non-compliance with the marketing authorisation or product specification file, or any other serious quality problems) with a medicinal or investigational medicinal product which may result in the recall of the product or an abnormal restriction in the supply (recommended).

evidence.what: notifications to competent authorities
confirmed quality defect records

points.question: Where the authorities were not notified of marketed product that does not comply with the marketing authorisation, is the non-compliance within the Annex 16 limits for unplanned deviations (recommended)?
points.verify: Where concerned competent authorities are not notified of product on the market found to be non-compliant with the marketing authorisation, verify that the degree of non-compliance satisfies the Annex 16 restrictions regarding the handling of unplanned deviations (recommended).

evidence.what: records of such non-compliance and its assessment

points.question: For outsourced activities, does a contract set out each party's role and responsibilities for defective products (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in case of outsourced activities, a contract describes the role and responsibilities of the manufacturer, the marketing authorisation holder and/or sponsor and any other relevant third parties in relation to assessment, decision-making, and dissemination of information and implementation of risk-reducing actions relating to a defective product (recommended).

evidence.what: contracts for outsourced activities

points.question: Do the contracts for outsourced activities say how to reach the responsible people at each party for quality defect and recall matters (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that such contracts (guidance in relation to contracts is provided in Chapter 7) also address how to contact those responsible at each party for the management of quality defect and recall issues (recommended).

evidence.what: contracts for outsourced activities

points.question: Are the people who manage complaint and quality defect investigations, and decide on risk measures including recalls, suitably trained and experienced (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that appropriately trained and experienced personnel are responsible for managing complaint and quality defect investigations and for deciding the measures to be taken to manage any potential risk(s) presented by those issues, including recalls (recommended).

evidence.what: document naming the responsible personnel
training and experience records of these personnel

points.question: Are these persons independent of sales and marketing, or is any exception justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the persons responsible for managing complaint and quality defect investigations and deciding the measures are independent of the sales and marketing organisation, unless otherwise justified (recommended).

evidence.what: organisation chart or document showing reporting lines
justification where not independent

points.question: If the Qualified Person who certified the batch is not among these persons, is that Qualified Person formally and promptly told of investigations, risk-reducing actions and recalls (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, if these persons do not include the Qualified Person involved in the certification for release of the concerned batch or batches, the Qualified Person is made formally aware of any investigations, any risk-reducing actions and any recall operations, in a timely manner (recommended).

evidence.what: records of formal communication to the Qualified Person

points.question: Are enough trained people and resources provided to handle, assess, investigate and review complaints and quality defects and to carry out risk-reducing actions (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that sufficient trained personnel and resources are made available for the handling, assessment, investigation and review of complaints and quality defects and for implementing any risk-reducing actions (recommended).

evidence.what: training records of personnel handling complaints and quality defects
staff on personnel and resources available for this work

points.question: Are enough trained people and resources also available to manage dealings with competent authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that sufficient trained personnel and resources are also available for the management of interactions with competent authorities (recommended).

evidence.what: training records of personnel managing interactions with competent authorities
staff on personnel and resources available for this work

points.question: Has the use of inter-disciplinary teams, including suitably trained Quality Management staff, been considered (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the use of inter-disciplinary teams, including appropriately trained Quality Management personnel, is considered (recommended).

evidence.what: procedure or records showing inter-disciplinary teams were considered

points.question: Where complaints and quality defects are handled centrally in the organisation, are the roles and responsibilities of the parties written down (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in situations in which complaint and quality defect handling is managed centrally within an organisation, the relative roles and responsibilities of the concerned parties are documented (recommended).

evidence.what: document of roles and responsibilities of the concerned parties

points.question: Where handling is managed centrally, do records show the investigation and management of issues was not delayed by it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that central management does not result in delays in the investigation and management of the issue (recommended).

evidence.what: complaint and quality defect records showing timelines

points.question: Is there a written procedure that tells staff what to do when a complaint comes in (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there are written procedures describing the actions to be taken upon receipt of a complaint (recommended).

evidence.what: complaint handling procedure

points.question: Do complaint records show that every complaint is written down and assessed for a possible quality defect or other issue (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all complaints are documented and assessed to establish if they represent a potential quality defect or other issue (recommended).

evidence.what: complaint records with their assessment

points.question: Do complaint and defect records show special care in finding out whether falsification is involved (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that special attention is given to establishing whether a complaint or suspected quality defect relates to falsification (recommended).

evidence.what: complaint and suspected quality defect records
complaint handling procedure

points.question: Are complaints that do not point to a possible quality defect recorded and passed to the right group or person (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that complaints which do not indicate a potential quality defect are documented appropriately and communicated to the relevant group or person responsible for the investigation and management of complaints of that nature, such as suspected adverse events (recommended).

evidence.what: records of complaints not indicating a quality defect
records of their communication to the responsible group or person

points.question: Are procedures in place for handling a request to investigate batch quality in support of a suspected adverse event investigation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there are procedures in place to facilitate a request to investigate the quality of a batch of a medicinal product in order to support an investigation into a reported suspected adverse event (recommended).

evidence.what: procedures for batch quality investigation requests

points.question: Do the procedures used when a quality defect investigation starts cover all the listed minimum topics (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when a quality defect investigation is initiated, procedures are in place to address at least: (i) the description of the reported quality defect; (ii) the determination of the extent of the quality defect, with the checking or testing of reference and/or retention samples considered as part of this and, in certain cases, a review of the batch production record, the batch certification record and the batch distribution records (especially for temperature-sensitive products) performed; (iii) the need to request a sample, or the return, of the defective product from the complainant and, where a sample is provided, the need for an appropriate evaluation to be carried out; (iv) the assessment of the risk(s) posed by the quality defect, based on its severity and extent; (v) the decision-making process to be used concerning the potential need for risk-reducing actions in the distribution network, such as batch or product recalls, or other actions; (vi) the assessment of the impact that any recall action may have on the availability of the medicinal product to patients/animals in any affected market, and the need to notify the relevant authorities of such impact; (vii) the internal and external communications to be made in relation to a quality defect and its investigation; (viii) the identification of the potential root cause(s) of the quality defect; (ix) the need for appropriate Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPAs) to be identified and implemented for the issue, and for the assessment of the effectiveness of those CAPAs (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation procedures

points.question: Do the records of reported possible quality defects keep all the original details (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the information reported in relation to possible quality defects is recorded, including all the original details (recommended).

evidence.what: records of reported possible quality defects

points.question: Do records show a risk-based assessment of how valid and how wide each reported quality defect is (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the validity and extent of all reported quality defects are documented and assessed in accordance with Quality Risk Management principles in order to support decisions regarding the degree of investigation and action taken (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect assessment records

points.question: Do defect investigation records show that other batches, and sometimes other products, were looked at (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, if a quality defect is discovered or suspected in a batch, consideration is given to checking other batches and in some cases other products, in order to determine whether they are also affected (recommended). Verify that, in particular, other batches which may contain portions of the defective batch or defective components are investigated (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records

points.question: Do defect investigations look back at earlier defect reports and other relevant information for signs of repeating problems (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that quality defect investigations include a review of previous quality defect reports or any other relevant information for any indication of specific or recurring problems requiring attention and possibly further regulatory action (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records

points.question: Do investigation records show decisions that match the risk and the seriousness of the non-compliance, and that were made in time (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the decisions made during and following quality defect investigations reflect the level of risk presented by the quality defect as well as the seriousness of any non-compliance with respect to the requirements of the marketing authorisation/product specification file or GMP (recommended). Verify that such decisions are timely to ensure that patient and animal safety is maintained, in a way that is commensurate with the level of risk presented by those issues (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation and decision records

points.question: When full information is not yet available early in an investigation, are suitable risk-reducing actions still taken at a suitable point (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, as comprehensive information on the nature and extent of the quality defect may not always be available at the early stages of an investigation, the decision-making processes still ensure that appropriate risk-reducing actions are taken at an appropriate time-point during such investigations (recommended).

evidence.what: decision-making process for quality defects
quality defect investigation and decision records

points.question: Is every decision and measure taken because of a quality defect written down (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all the decisions and measures taken as a result of a quality defect are documented (recommended).

evidence.what: records of decisions and measures for quality defects

points.question: Do records show timely reporting of quality defects that may lead to a recall or an abnormal supply restriction (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that quality defects are reported in a timely manner by the manufacturer to the marketing authorisation holder/sponsor and all concerned Competent Authorities in cases where the quality defect may result in the recall of the product or in an abnormal restriction in the supply of the product (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect reports sent to the marketing authorisation holder/sponsor and Competent Authorities

points.question: Do defect investigation records show a suitable depth of root cause analysis (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that an appropriate level of root cause analysis work is applied during the investigation of quality defects (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records

points.question: Where human error is given as the cause of a defect, is this formally justified and were other causes not missed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where human error is suspected or identified as the cause of a quality defect, this is formally justified and care is exercised so as to ensure that process, procedural or system-based errors or problems are not overlooked, if present (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records citing human error

points.question: Do records show suitable CAPAs for each quality defect and a check of how well they worked (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that appropriate CAPAs are identified and taken in response to a quality defect (recommended). Verify that the effectiveness of such actions is monitored and assessed (recommended).

evidence.what: CAPA records for quality defects
records of CAPA effectiveness monitoring and assessment

points.question: Are quality defect records reviewed and trended regularly to spot repeating problems (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that quality defect records are reviewed and trend analyses are performed regularly for any indication of specific or recurring problems requiring attention (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect record reviews and trend analyses

points.question: Where the true root cause of a quality defect could not be determined, do the records show that thought was given to identifying and addressing the most likely root cause(s) (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in cases where the true root cause(s) of the quality defect cannot be determined, consideration is given to identifying the most likely root cause(s) and to addressing those (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect investigation records

points.question: Are there written procedures for recalls and other risk-reducing actions, kept under regular review (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that there are established written procedures, regularly reviewed and updated when necessary, in order to undertake any recall activity or implement any other risk-reducing actions (recommended).

evidence.what: recall and risk-reducing action procedures
review and update history of these procedures

points.question: Is every retrieval of marketed product from distribution because of a quality defect handled as a recall (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, after a product has been placed on the market, any retrieval of it from the distribution network as a result of a quality defect is regarded and managed as a recall (recommended). This does not apply to the retrieval (or return) of samples of the product from the distribution network to facilitate an investigation into a quality defect issue/report (recommended).

evidence.what: recall procedure
records of product retrievals from the distribution network

points.question: Can a recall be started quickly and at any time (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that recall operations are capable of being initiated promptly and at any time (recommended).

evidence.what: recall procedure
staff responsible for recalls on how a recall is started

points.question: Can the people in charge of recalls readily get distribution records with enough customer details (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the batch/product distribution records are readily available to the persons responsible for recalls, and contain sufficient information on wholesalers and directly supplied customers (with addresses, phone and/or fax numbers inside and outside working hours, batches and amounts delivered), including those for exported products and medical samples (recommended).

evidence.what: batch/product distribution records
access of persons responsible for recalls to these records

points.question: For investigational medicinal products, are all trial sites and destination countries shown (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of investigational medicinal products, all trial sites are identified and the countries of destination are indicated (recommended).

evidence.what: distribution records of investigational medicinal products

points.question: For an investigational product that also has a marketing authorisation, is the authorisation holder told of related quality defects (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of an investigational medicinal product for which a marketing authorisation has been issued, the manufacturer of the investigational medicinal product, in cooperation with the sponsor, informs the marketing authorisation holder of any quality defect that could be related to the authorised medicinal product (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect communications to the marketing authorisation holder

points.question: Has the sponsor put in place a rapid unblinding procedure that reveals product identity only as far as needed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the sponsor has implemented a procedure for the rapid unblinding of blinded products, where this is necessary for a prompt recall (recommended). Verify that the sponsor ensures that the procedure discloses the identity of the blinded product only in so far as is necessary (recommended).

evidence.what: sponsor's rapid unblinding procedure

points.question: Do recall records show that the depth of the recall in the distribution network was considered after consulting the authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that consideration is given, following consultation with the concerned Competent Authorities, as to how far into the distribution network a recall action should extend, taking into account the potential risk to public or animal health and any impact that the proposed recall action may have (recommended).

evidence.what: recall decision records
consultation with the concerned Competent Authorities

points.question: Are the authorities told when no recall is proposed for a defective batch because it has expired (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the Competent Authorities are also informed in situations in which no recall action is being proposed for a defective batch because the batch has expired (such as with short shelf-life products) (recommended).

evidence.what: communications to the Competent Authorities on expired defective batches

points.question: Do records show that the authorities concerned were told before a planned recall (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that all concerned Competent Authorities are informed in advance in cases where products are intended to be recalled (recommended).

evidence.what: recall notifications to the concerned Competent Authorities

points.question: Where rapid actions for very serious issues come before notifying the authorities, was advance agreement tried wherever possible (recommended)?
points.verify: Where, for very serious issues (i.e. those with the potential to seriously impact upon patient or animal health), rapid risk-reducing actions (such as a product recall) are taken in advance of notifying the Competent Authorities, verify that, wherever possible, attempts are made to agree these in advance of their execution with the concerned Competent Authorities (recommended).

evidence.what: records of rapid risk-reducing actions
communications with the concerned Competent Authorities

points.question: Do recall records show a check for different effects in different markets and, if so, market-specific actions discussed with the authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that it is also considered whether the proposed recall action may affect different markets in different ways, and, if this is the case, that appropriate market-specific risk-reducing actions are developed and discussed with the concerned competent authorities (recommended).

evidence.what: recall decision records
discussions with the concerned competent authorities

points.question: Before deciding on a recall or similar action, is the shortage risk weighed for a product with no authorised alternative (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, taking account of its therapeutic use, the risk of shortage of a medicinal product which has no authorised alternative is considered before deciding on a risk-reducing action such as a recall (recommended).

evidence.what: decision records for risk-reducing actions

points.question: Is any decision not to carry out a risk-reducing action agreed beforehand with the competent authority (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any decisions not to execute a risk-reducing action which would otherwise be needed are agreed with the competent authority in advance (recommended).

evidence.what: competent authority agreement on file
decision records for risk-reducing actions

points.question: Are recalled products marked and kept apart in a secure area until their fate is decided (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that recalled products are identified and stored separately in a secure area while awaiting a decision on their fate (recommended).

evidence.what: storage area for recalled products
records of recalled product storage

points.question: Is there a formal, written disposition for every recalled batch (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that a formal disposition of all recalled batches is made and documented (recommended).

evidence.what: disposition records of recalled batches

points.question: Is the reason for any rework of recalled products written down and discussed with the authority (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the rationale for any decision to rework recalled products is documented and discussed with the relevant competent authority (recommended).

evidence.what: documented rationale for rework of recalled products
discussion with the relevant competent authority

points.question: For reworked batches that may go back on the market, is the remaining shelf-life taken into account (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the extent of shelf-life remaining for any reworked batches that are being considered for placement onto the market is also considered (recommended).

evidence.what: decision records for reworked recalled batches

points.question: Is each recall tracked in writing to closure, ending with a final report that reconciles quantities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the progress of the recall process is recorded until closure and a final report is issued, including a reconciliation between the delivered and recovered quantities of the concerned products/batches (recommended).

evidence.what: recall progress records
final recall reports with reconciliation

points.question: Are the recall arrangements evaluated from time to time, for office and out-of-office hours, with the evaluation written down and justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the effectiveness of the arrangements in place for recalls is periodically evaluated to confirm that they remain robust and fit for use; that such evaluations extend to both within office-hour situations and out-of-office hour situations and that, when performing them, consideration is given as to whether mock-recall actions should be performed; and that this evaluation is documented and justified (recommended).

evidence.what: documented evaluations of recall arrangements

points.question: Are risk-reducing actions other than recalls looked at case by case and discussed with the authorities (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that other potential risk-reducing actions are considered on a case-by-case basis and discussed with the concerned competent authorities (recommended).

evidence.what: decision records for risk-reducing actions
discussions with the concerned competent authorities

points.question: Can a recall be started before the cause and full size of the defect are known, when health protection needs it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in certain cases where this is needed to protect public or animal health, recall operations can be initiated prior to establishing the root cause(s) and full extent of the quality defect (recommended).

evidence.what: recall procedure
records of recall operations

points.question: In a serious or possibly life-threatening case, do records show that the authorities were told and asked for advice (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the event of a serious or potentially life-threatening situation, local, national, and/or international authorities are informed and their advice is sought (recommended).

evidence.what: records of informing authorities and seeking their advice
procedure for serious or potentially life-threatening situations

points.question: Where complaints, defects and recalls are managed centrally, are each party's roles written down and are delays avoided (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the management of complaints, quality defects and recalls is performed centrally, the relative roles and responsibilities of the concerned parties are documented and that such central management does not result in delays in the investigation and management of the issue (recommended).

complaint, quality defect and recall records showing timelines

points.question: Is there evidence that the MAH is satisfied with the centralised way quality defects are handled, including the contact persons (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH is satisfied with the centralised arrangements that are in place for handling quality defects, such as within corporate quality groups or at manufacturing site(s), including the arrangements regarding the contact persons who may communicate quality defect issues to the competent authorities (and the EMA in the case of products authorised via the Centralised Procedure) (recommended).

evidence.what: centralised quality defect handling arrangements
records showing the MAH is satisfied with these arrangements

points.question: Does the applicant/MAH have a named contact person for product defects and recalls, given in the MA application form (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the applicant/MAH has, as expected, a dedicated responsible person to serve as a contact person for product defects and recalls in the post-authorisation phase, and that the applicant/MAH has, as expected, provided information on its contact person in the MA-application form (Ref. MA Application Form in Notice to Applicants Volume 2B, Article 6 of Regulation 726/2004, Annex I to Directive 2001/83/EC, Volume 6B of the Notice to Applicants, and Annex II of Regulation 6/2019) (recommended).

evidence.what: designation of the contact person for product defects and recalls
MA-application form

points.question: Have the MAH, the manufacturer and the other parties set out and agreed who does what for defective medicinal products?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH, the manufacturer and other parties have defined and agreed their respective roles and responsibilities with regard to quality defective medicinal products.

evidence.what: agreed roles and responsibilities between the parties

points.question: For outsourced activities, does the contract set out each party's role for defective products and how to reach the responsible people (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in case of outsourced activities, a contract describes the role and responsibilities of the manufacturer, the marketing authorisation holder and/or sponsor and any other relevant third parties in relation to assessment, decision-making, and dissemination of information and implementation of risk-reducing actions relating to a defective product (recommended). evidence.what: contracts for outsourced activities

points.question: Do records show timely reporting of quality defects that may lead to a recall or an abnormal supply restriction (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that quality defects are reported in a timely manner by the manufacturer to the marketing authorisation holder/sponsor and all concerned Competent Authorities in cases where the quality defect may result in the recall of the product or in an abnormal restriction in the supply of the product (recommended).

evidence.what: quality defect reports sent to the marketing authorisation holder/sponsor and Competent Authorities

points.question: For an investigational product that also has a marketing authorisation, is the authorisation holder told of related quality defects (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in the case of an investigational medicinal product for which a marketing authorisation has been issued, the manufacturer of the investigational medicinal product, in cooperation with the sponsor, informs the marketing authorisation holder of any quality defect that could be related to the authorised medicinal product (recommended).

points.question: Does the manufacturer at once tell the competent authority and the MAH when information points to a falsified or suspected falsified product?

evidence.what: procedure for reporting falsified or suspected falsified products
notifications to the competent authority and the MAH

points.question: Does the MAH have a system to take in defect and falsification reports from manufacturers and respond suitably (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has a system in place to receive quality defect and product falsification reports from manufacturers and that it is able to respond to them in a manner that is appropriate (recommended).

points.question: Does the MAH have systems for dealing with adverse reaction reports?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has systems in place to deal with adverse reaction reports, as the EU pharmacovigilance legislation obliges it to.

points.question: Does the MAH have robust procedures for managing product recalls (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the MAH has robust procedures for the management of product recalls (recommended).

points.question: Are the recall arrangements checked from time to time to confirm they still work well (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the effectiveness of the arrangements in place for recalls is periodically evaluated to confirm that they remain robust and fit for use (recommended).

points.question: Do the evaluations of recall arrangements cover office and out-of-office hours, weigh up mock recalls, and are they written down and justified?
points.verify: Verify that the evaluations of recall arrangements extend to both within office-hour situations as well as out-of-office hour situations and that, when performing such evaluations, consideration is given as to whether mock-recall actions should be performed. evidence.what: documented evaluations of recall arrangements

points.question: Has the MAH told the Member States concerned straight away about each step to stop or withdraw a product, with the reasons and the stated grounds?

points.question: For veterinary products, does the product database hold the market dates, availability details and any suspension or revocation dates entered by the MAH?

points.question: For veterinary products, has the MAH promptly told the authority about outside bans or limits, new benefit-risk information and any planned stop of marketing?

points.question: Are returned products that were outside the manufacturer's control labelled as returned and kept apart from clinical use (recommended)?

points.question: Is there a system that makes sure every quality complaint, spoken or written, is logged and fully investigated (recommended)?

evidence.what: records of education, training and experience of supervisors

points.question: Are there enough qualified people to carry out and supervise the work on each drug product?
points.verify: Verify that there is an adequate number of qualified personnel to perform and supervise the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of each drug product.

evidence.what: staffing of manufacture, processing, packing and holding
records showing number of qualified personnel

points.question: Do staff working with drug products wear clean clothing that fits their duties?
points.verify: Verify that personnel engaged in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product wear clean clothing appropriate for the duties they perform.

points.question: Is protective apparel worn as needed to keep drug products free from contamination?

points.question: Is anyone found to have an apparent illness or open lesions kept from direct contact with materials and products until cleared?

evidence.what: records showing exclusion and return of such persons
