points.question: Before processing starts, are steps taken to make sure the work area and equipment are clean and cleared of leftovers (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, before any processing operation is started, steps are taken to ensure that the work area and equipment are clean and free from any starting materials, products, product residues or documents not needed for the current operation (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the steps taken before start of processing
work area and equipment before a processing operation starts

points.question: Have the critical processes been validated (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that critical processes are validated (see "Validation" in this Chapter) (recommended).

evidence.what: validation records of critical processes

points.question: Do records show that rejected products are reprocessed only as an exception (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the reprocessing of rejected products is exceptional (recommended).

evidence.what: records of reprocessing of rejected products

points.question: Is reprocessing of rejected products done only when quality, specifications, procedure and risk evaluation conditions are all met?
points.verify: Verify that reprocessing of rejected products is done only if the quality of the final product is not affected, if the specifications are met and if it is done in accordance with a defined and authorised procedure after evaluation of the risks involved.

evidence.what: defined and authorised reprocessing procedure
risk evaluation and results against specifications for reprocessed products

points.question: Is a record kept of each reprocessing (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that record is kept of the reprocessing (recommended).

evidence.what: reprocessing records

points.question: Does Quality Control consider whether extra testing is needed for reprocessed finished product or product containing recovered material (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the need for additional testing of any finished product which has been reprocessed, or into which a recovered product has been incorporated, is considered by the Quality Control Department (recommended).

evidence.what: Quality Control Department consideration of additional testing for such finished products

points.question: Is recovery of earlier batches into a batch of the same product authorised before it is done (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the recovery of all or part of earlier batches which conform to the needed quality by incorporation into a batch of the same product at a defined stage of manufacture is authorised beforehand (recommended).

evidence.what: prior authorisation of recovery

points.question: Is recovery done to a defined procedure after the risks, including shelf life effects, were evaluated (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the recovery is carried out in accordance with a defined procedure after evaluation of the risks involved, including any possible effect on shelf life (recommended).

evidence.what: defined procedure for recovery
evaluation of the risks of recovery, including effect on shelf life

points.question: Do records exist for each recovery (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the recovery is recorded (recommended).

evidence.what: recovery records

points.question: Are containers holding subdivided material suitable and identified with the listed details (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, if a material is subdivided for later use in production operations, the container receiving the material is suitable and is so identified that the following information is available: material name and/or item code; receiving or control number; weight or measure of material in the new container; and re-evaluation or retest date if appropriate (recommended).

evidence.what: containers of subdivided material and their identification

points.question: Are critical weighing, measuring or subdividing steps witnessed or given an equal control (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that critical weighing, measuring, or subdividing operations are witnessed or subjected to an equivalent control (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the witness or equivalent control of these operations
critical weighing, measuring or subdividing operations

points.question: Do production staff check before use that the materials match the batch record (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, prior to use, production personnel verify that the materials are those specified in the batch record for the intended intermediate or API (recommended).

evidence.what: batch records showing the material check before use
production personnel on checking materials before use

points.question: Do other critical activities have a witness or an equal control (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that other critical activities are witnessed or subjected to an equivalent control (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the witness or equivalent control of other critical activities

points.question: Are suitable controls in place at every manufacturing stage to protect intermediate and API quality (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that appropriate controls are established at all stages of manufacturing to assure intermediate and/or API quality (recommended).

evidence.what: documents describing the process controls
records showing the process controls applied

points.question: Are steps before cell culture or fermentation, such as cell banking, done under suitable process controls (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that steps prior to the cell culture/fermentation step (e.g. cell banking) are performed under appropriate process controls (recommended).

evidence.what: documents describing controls for prior steps
records of prior steps showing the controls

points.question: Do the process controls consider upkeep of the working cell bank and correct inoculation and culture expansion (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in general, process controls take into account maintenance of the Working Cell Bank (where appropriate) and proper inoculation and expansion of the culture (recommended).

evidence.what: documents describing the process controls
records showing the process controls applied

points.question: Do the process controls consider critical operating parameters and the monitoring of growth, viability and productivity (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in general, process controls take into account control of the critical operating parameters during fermentation/cell culture, and monitoring of the process for cell growth, viability (for most cell culture processes) and productivity where appropriate (recommended).

evidence.what: documents describing the process controls
records showing the process controls applied

points.question: Do the process controls consider how harvest and purification remove unwanted material while protecting the product (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in general, process controls take into account harvest and purification procedures that remove cells, cellular debris and media components while protecting the intermediate or API from contamination (particularly of a microbiological nature) and from loss of quality (recommended).

evidence.what: documents describing the process controls
records showing the process controls applied

points.question: Do the process controls consider bioburden and endotoxin monitoring and viral safety (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in general, process controls take into account monitoring of bioburden and, where needed, endotoxin levels at appropriate stages of production, and viral safety concerns as described in ICH Guideline Q5A Quality of Biotechnological Products: Viral Safety Evaluation of Biotechnology Products Derived from Cell Lines of Human or Animal Origin (recommended).

evidence.what: documents describing the process controls
records showing the process controls applied

points.question: Do records show that the critical operating parameters are watched so the run stays in line with the set process (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that critical operating parameters (for example temperature, pH, agitation rates, addition of gases, pressure) are monitored to ensure consistency with the established process (recommended).

evidence.what: monitoring records of critical operating parameters
monitoring of parameters during fermentation/cell culture

points.question: Do records show monitoring of cell growth, viability and, where it fits, productivity (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that cell growth, viability (for most cell culture processes), and, where appropriate, productivity are also monitored (recommended).

evidence.what: monitoring records of cell growth, viability and productivity

points.question: Are suitable precautions in place so that virus cannot be carried from steps before viral removal or inactivation to steps after it (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that appropriate precautions are taken to prevent potential viral contamination from pre-viral to post-viral removal/inactivation steps (recommended).

evidence.what: documents describing the precautions
precautions between pre-viral and post-viral steps

points.question: Is open processing done in areas kept apart from other processing, with their own air handling units (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that open processing is performed in areas that are separate from other processing activities and have separate air handling units (recommended).

evidence.what: areas used for open processing and their air handling units
layout and air handling drawings of these areas

points.question: Do the controls for clinical trial APIs match the development stage of the drug product that contains the API (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the controls used in the manufacture of APIs for use in clinical trials are consistent with the stage of development of the drug product incorporating the API (recommended).

evidence.what: documents describing the controls for clinical trial APIs

points.question: Can process and test procedures be changed as process knowledge grows and clinical testing moves forward (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that process and test procedures are flexible to provide for changes as knowledge of the process increases and clinical testing of a drug product progresses from pre-clinical stages through clinical stages (recommended).

evidence.what: process and test procedures

points.question: Once the API is made for drug products meant for clinical trials, is it made in suitable facilities under proper production and control procedures (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, once drug development reaches the stage where the API is produced for use in drug products intended for clinical trials, the manufacturer ensures that APIs are manufactured in suitable facilities using appropriate production and control procedures to ensure the quality of the API (recommended).

evidence.what: facilities used for these APIs
production and control procedures

points.question: Is cross-contaminant presence in shared facilities handled according to its risk, linked to levels safe for all populations (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the presence of cross-contaminants from different medicinal products produced in shared facilities is managed according to the risk posed, which in turn is related to levels that can be considered safe for all populations (recommended).

evidence.what: documents showing how cross-contaminant risk is managed

points.question: Are health based limits, from a derived safe threshold value, used to identify the cross-contamination risks (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that health based limits through the derivation of a safe threshold value are employed to identify the risks posed (recommended).

evidence.what: documents showing the health based limits used to identify risks

points.question: Does each threshold value come from a structured scientific review of all available pharmacological and toxicological data (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the derivation of the threshold value (e.g. permitted daily exposure (PDE) or threshold of toxicological concern (TTC)) is the result of a structured scientific evaluation of all available pharmacological and toxicological data including both non-clinical and clinical data (recommended).

evidence.what: documents showing how the threshold value was derived

points.question: Where the guideline's main approach for deriving safe threshold levels is not followed, is this adequately justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Where there is a deviation from the main approach highlighted in the guideline to derive safe threshold levels, verify that it is adequately justified (recommended).

evidence.what: justification for the deviation

points.question: Where safe threshold levels are derived in a way that departs from the guideline's main approach, is this adequately justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Where there is a deviation from the main approach highlighted in the guideline to derive safe threshold levels, verify that it is adequately justified (recommended).

evidence.what: justification for the deviation

points.question: Do the PDE documents show all four steps of the determination?
points.verify: Verify that determination of a PDE involves (i) hazard identification by reviewing all relevant data, (ii) identification of "critical effects", (iii) determination of the no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) of the findings that are considered to be critical effects, and (iv) use of several adjustment factors to account for various uncertainties.

evidence.what: documents showing how the PDE was derived

points.question: Is the PDE worked out with the stated equation?
points.verify: Verify that the PDE is derived as PDE = (NOAEL x Weight Adjustment) / (F1 x F2 x F3 x F4 x F5).

evidence.what: PDE calculation

points.question: Are PDEs derived on the assumption of human exposure (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that PDEs are derived assuming human exposure, as is considered pragmatic (recommended).

evidence.what: documents showing how the PDE was derived

points.question: Is the acceptable contamination level worked out from the human PDE, also for veterinary products?
points.verify: Verify that the level of contamination that can be accepted is calculated from the human PDE, even when the product that will be contaminated is a veterinary medicinal product.

evidence.what: calculation of the acceptable contamination level

points.question: Does the derivation of limits consider the dose to be given?
points.verify: Verify that the derivation of limits takes account of the dose to be administered, which will be influenced by the body weight of the species to be treated.

evidence.what: documents showing how the limits were derived

points.question: Is the PDE calculated per kg body weight and not per person (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the PDE is calculated on a mg/kg bw basis (i.e. using a weight adjustment figure of 1) rather than on a per person basis (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE calculation

points.question: For veterinary products given to food producing animals, does the carryover limit consider both target animal safety and consumer safety?
points.verify: Verify that, when the product that may become contaminated with a residual active substance is a veterinary medicinal product for administration to food producing animals, the carryover limit applied takes account of both target animal safety considerations and consumer safety considerations.

evidence.what: documents showing how the carryover limit was set

points.question: Is it shown, using worst case exposure scenarios, that the target animal and the consumer stay at or below the PDE (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that it is demonstrated, based on worst case exposure scenarios, that neither the target animal nor the consumer will be exposed to residual active substance levels exceeding the PDE (recommended).

evidence.what: documents showing the worst case exposure assessment

points.question: Where another approach is used to set health based exposure limits, is it adequately and scientifically justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Where other approaches are used to determine health based exposure limits, verify that this is adequately and scientifically justified (recommended).

evidence.what: justification for the other approach

points.question: Was all available animal and human data reviewed for each compound to identify its hazards (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, for hazard identification, a review of all available animal and human data is performed for each compound (recommended).

evidence.what: hazard identification data review for each compound

points.question: Where data sets are incomplete, are the gaps critically assessed for their effect on a reliable limit?
points.verify: Verify that, if data sets are incomplete, the identified gaps are critically assessed with regard to the impact this might have on deriving a reliable health based exposure limit.

evidence.what: assessment of the identified data gaps

points.question: Does the data used for hazard identification include the named non-clinical data and study types and clinical data (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that data for hazard identification include non-clinical pharmacodynamic data, repeat-dose toxicity studies, carcinogenicity studies, in vitro and in vivo genotoxicity studies, reproductive and developmental toxicity studies as well as clinical data (therapeutic and adverse effects) (recommended).

evidence.what: hazard identification data for the compound

points.question: Do the critical effects include the most sensitive adverse-effect indicator from non-clinical toxicity studies, unless clearly shown not relevant?
points.verify: Verify that critical effects include the most sensitive indicator of an adverse effect seen in non-clinical toxicity studies unless there is clear evidence (e.g. from mechanistic studies, pharmacodynamic data etc.) that such findings are not relevant to humans or the target animal.

evidence.what: documents showing the critical effects identified

points.question: Are clinical therapeutic and adverse effects also treated as critical effects?
points.verify: Verify that critical effects also include any clinical therapeutic and adverse effect.

evidence.what: documents showing the critical effects identified

points.question: Has a NOAEL been set for every critical effect identified (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that a NOAEL is established for all critical effects identified (recommended).

evidence.what: documents showing the NOAELs established

points.question: Where several animal studies show the critical effect, is the NOAEL at the lowest dose used for the PDE (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, if the critical effect is observed in several animal studies, the NOAEL occurring at the lowest dose is used for calculation of the PDE value (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE calculation

points.question: Does a NOAEL taken from clinical pharmacodynamic effects match the highest tested dose seen as having no therapeutic effect (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that a NOAEL based on clinical pharmacodynamic effects corresponds to the highest dose tested which is considered therapeutically inefficacious (recommended).

evidence.what: documents showing the NOAELs established

points.question: Is the PDE obtained by dividing the critical-effect NOAEL by adjustment factors?
points.verify: Verify that the PDE is derived by dividing the NOAEL for the critical effect by various adjustment factors (also referred to as safety-, uncertainty-, assessment- or modifying factors) to account for various uncertainties and to allow extrapolation to a reliable and robust no-effect level in the human or target animal population.

evidence.what: PDE calculation showing the adjustment factors

points.question: Do the factors F1, F2 and F3 used in the PDE calculation have the stated values and purposes?
points.verify: Verify that F1 is a factor (values between 2 and 12) to account for extrapolation between species, F2 is a factor of 10 to account for variability between individuals, and F3 is a factor 10 to account for repeat-dose toxicity studies of short duration, i.e., less than 4-weeks.

evidence.what: PDE calculation showing the adjustment factors

points.question: Where F4 is applied, is it a factor of 1-10 used for severe toxicity (recommended)?
points.verify: Where F4 is applied, verify that it is a factor (1-10) applied in cases of severe toxicity, e.g. non-genotoxic carcinogenicity, neurotoxicity or teratogenicity (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE calculation showing the adjustment factors

points.question: Where F5 is applied, is it used because no no-effect level was established (recommended)?
points.verify: Where F5 is applied, verify that it is a variable factor applied if the no-effect level was not established (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE calculation showing the adjustment factors

points.question: Where only an LOEL is available and a factor is used for this, is it up to 10 and based on how severe the toxicity is (recommended)?
points.verify: Where only an LOEL is available and a factor is used, verify that it is a factor of up to 10 depending on the severity of the toxicity (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE calculation showing the adjustment factors

points.question: Where extra modifying factors are used for remaining uncertainties, are they backed by literature data and an adequate discussion (recommended)?
points.verify: Where additional modifying factors are used to address residual uncertainties not covered by the above factors, verify that they are well supported with literature data and an adequate discussion is provided to support their use, e.g. lack of data for reproductive and developmental toxicity (see section 5.4) (recommended).

evidence.what: literature data and discussion supporting the additional factors

points.question: Is there a justification for which adjustment factors were used and their values (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the use and choice of adjustment factors are justified (recommended).

evidence.what: justification of the adjustment factors

points.question: Where adjustment factors differ from the default values, is this adequately and scientifically justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Where there are deviations from the default values for the adjustment factors presented above, verify that they are adequately and scientifically justified (recommended).

evidence.what: justification for deviating from default values

points.question: Where more than one PDE value was calculated, do records show which PDE was chosen for cleaning validation and why (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, if several critical effects have been identified resulting in calculation of more than one PDE value, a decision on the most appropriate PDE to be used for the cleaning validation process is made with an appropriate justification, and that usually, by default, the lowest PDE value is used (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE calculation showing all PDE values
decision on final PDE with justification

points.question: Does the critical effect identification take clinical data on the active substance into account (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that clinical pharmacological data are considered when identifying the critical effect, and that consideration is given to what extent the active substance in question has been associated with critical adverse effects in the clinical setting (recommended).

evidence.what: critical effect identification for the active substance

points.question: Are correction factors used when the route of administration changes and bioavailability clearly differs (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that correction factors for route-to-route extrapolation are applied if there are clear differences (e.g. > 40%) in route-specific bioavailability (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE calculation with route-to-route extrapolation

points.question: Is each route-to-route extrapolation worked out for the individual case?
points.verify: Verify that the route-to-route extrapolation is performed on a case-by-case basis.

evidence.what: PDE calculation with route-to-route extrapolation

points.question: Are the route-to-route correction factors preferably based on human data, or target animal data for veterinary products (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the correction factors for route-to-route extrapolation are preferably based on human data or, in the case of veterinary medicinal products, data in the relevant target animal (recommended).

evidence.what: data used for the correction factors

points.question: For veterinary products that may be contaminated, is the TTC applied on a per kg bodyweight basis (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when the product that may become contaminated with a residual active substance is a veterinary medicinal product, the same TTC is used but expressed on a 'per kg bodyweight' basis (i.e. the TTC is 0.03 µg/kg bw/day) (recommended).

evidence.what: limit setting for the residual active substance

points.question: For products given to food producing animals, does the carryover limit cover both the animal's safety and the consumer's safety?
points.verify: Verify that, when the contaminated product is for administration to food producing animals, the carryover limit applied takes account of both target animal safety considerations and consumer safety considerations.

evidence.what: carryover limit setting

points.question: Is there a worst case demonstration that target animal and consumer exposure stays within the TTC (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that it is demonstrated, based on worst case exposure scenarios, that neither the target animal nor the consumer will be exposed to residual active substance levels exceeding the TTC (recommended).

evidence.what: worst case exposure demonstration

points.question: Where enough carcinogenicity data exist for a genotoxic active substance, is a compound-specific risk assessment used in place of the TTC approach (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, for genotoxic active substances where sufficient carcinogenicity data exists, compound-specific risk assessments to derive acceptable intakes are applied instead of the TTC-based acceptable intake approach (recommended).

evidence.what: risk assessment deriving the acceptable intake

points.question: Where the PDE approach is used for a genotoxic substance, is it backed by enough evidence of a threshold mechanism (recommended)?
points.verify: Where the PDE approach is used to establish safe exposure levels without appreciable risk of genotoxicity for a genotoxic pharmaceutical substance, verify that there is sufficient evidence of a threshold related mechanism (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE document for the genotoxic substance

points.question: Are highly sensitising products made in dedicated facilities when no acceptable exposure level is supported or the handling risk cannot be controlled?
points.verify: Verify that, as outlined in Chapter 3 paragraph 3.6 of the GMP guideline, dedicated facilities are used for manufacturing active substances and medicinal products with a high sensitising potential for which scientific data does not support an acceptable level of exposure or the risk associated with handling the product at the facility cannot be adequately controlled by organisational or technical measures.

evidence.what: facilities where highly sensitising products are made
records showing which facilities make these products

points.question: Does the classification of high sensitising potential look at how often sensitisation occurs in humans, or its likelihood from animal data or other validated tests (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that classification of an active substance or medicinal product with a high sensitising potential considers whether the substance shows a high frequency of sensitising occurrence in humans, or a probability of occurrence of a high sensitisation rate in humans based on animal data or other validated tests (recommended).

evidence.what: classification of sensitising potential

points.question: Is the severity of the sensitising reactions part of the weight of evidence assessment (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the severity of these reactions is also considered and is included in a weight of evidence assessment (recommended).

evidence.what: weight of evidence assessment

points.question: Where other possible cross-contamination routes exist, are their risks looked at for each case (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where other potential routes of cross-contamination exist, the risks posed are considered on a case-by-case basis (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing the risks considered for each case

points.question: Is residual active substance brought down to a level without risk to reproduction and development (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in order to ensure protection of all populations, the presence of residual active substance is reduced to a level that will not pose a risk for effects on reproductive and developmental parameters (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing residual active substance levels and the reproductive and developmental risk

points.question: Where a sub-chronic/chronic study NOAEL with an extra adjustment factor is used for the PDE, is this justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Where, in these cases of missing data on reproductive and developmental toxicity, the NOAEL of a sub-chronic/chronic study is used in the calculation of a PDE with application of an additional adjustment factor (e.g. 10), verify that this is adequately justified (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE calculation with its justification

points.question: Where a class-specific profile is used by read across for an untested contaminant, are suitable study data on related compounds available (recommended)?
points.verify: Where a class-specific profile is used for hazard identification of the not tested contaminant through application of a read across approach, verify that appropriate data from reproductive and developmental toxicity studies of related compounds are available (recommended).

evidence.what: hazard identification with the related compound data

points.question: Where default value categories are used to set exposure limits for early phase IMPs, is this approach justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Where estimation of PDEs is apparently difficult and an alternative approach using categorisation into specific default value categories (e.g. based on low/high expected pharmacological potency, low/high toxicity, genotoxicity/carcinogenicity, similar to the tiered Threshold of Toxicological Concern approaches proposed by Kroes et al. (2004), Munro et al. (2008), and Dolan et al. (2005)) is used to derive health-based exposure limits, verify that it is adequately justified (recommended).

evidence.what: exposure limit derivation with its justification

points.question: Are compound-specific limits worked out once more pharmacological and toxicological data become available (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, with the availability of more pharmacological and toxicological data, compound-specific limits are calculated as described above for the derivation of health-based exposure limits (recommended).

evidence.what: exposure limit calculation for the compound

points.question: Was a full literature search done to identify the critical effects for the PDE (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the identification of critical effects in the establishment of a PDE as outlined in section 4 is based on a comprehensive literature search including handbook and monographs as well as searches in electronic scientific databases (recommended).

evidence.what: literature search for the PDE

points.question: Are the way the search was done and what it found written down clearly?
points.verify: Verify that the search strategy and the results of the search are clearly documented.

evidence.what: documented search strategy and search results

points.question: After expert review, does the company discuss the critical endpoints and explain its choice of endpoints and dose for the PDE (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, following an expert review, the company provides a discussion with respect to the critical endpoints of concern and their rationale for the choice of endpoints and dose that is to be used in the derivation of the PDE (recommended).

evidence.what: discussion of critical endpoints and rationale

points.question: Are the key studies behind the PDE traced to their original source and checked for quality (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the pivotal animal and human studies used for the derivation of the PDE are sourced to the original reference and reviewed regarding their quality (study design, description of finding, accuracy of the report etc.) (recommended).

evidence.what: references and quality review of the pivotal studies

points.question: Does the PDE strategy explain clearly why each adjustment factor was used (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the PDE determination strategy provides a clear rationale regarding the adjustment factors that were applied in deriving the PDE (recommended).

evidence.what: PDE determination strategy

points.question: Does the first page of each PDE strategy document summarise the assessment process (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in order to provide an overview to the GMP inspectors, the initial page of any prepared PDE determination strategy document is a summary of the assessment process (please see Annex for template example) (recommended).

evidence.what: initial page of PDE determination strategy document

points.question: For products already made in shared facilities, was the guidance applied or the existing arrangements justified within the set period (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, for medicinal products already produced in shared manufacturing facilities, the guidance took effect or existing arrangements were scientifically justified within 1 year after publication of the guideline for manufacturers of products for human use, including those who manufacture human and veterinary medicines using shared manufacturing facilities, and within 2 years after publication of the guideline for manufacturers solely producing products for veterinary use (recommended).

evidence.what: dated records showing application of the guidance or scientific justification of existing arrangements

points.question: Where antimicrobials are used, is manufacturing still done aseptically?
points.verify: Verify that the use of antimicrobials does not replace the requirement for aseptic manufacturing.

evidence.what: manufacturing steps where antimicrobials are used
manufacturing procedure

points.question: Are antimicrobials taken out as early as possible unless the authorisation foresees them in the finished product (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when antimicrobials are used, they are removed as soon as possible, unless the presence thereof in the finished product is specifically foreseen in the marketing authorisation/clinical trials authorisation (e.g. antibiotics that are part of the matrix of the finished product) (recommended).

evidence.what: manufacturing procedure showing removal step
marketing authorisation/clinical trials authorisation
batch records

points.question: Is it ensured that antibiotics or antimicrobials do not disturb the sterility test and are absent from the finished product unless the authorisation foresees them?
points.verify: Verify that it is ensured that antibiotics or antimicrobials do not interfere with the sterility testing, and that they are not present in the finished product (unless specifically foreseen in the marketing authorisation/clinical trial authorisation).

evidence.what: records showing no interference with sterility testing
records showing absence in the finished product
marketing authorisation/clinical trial authorisation

points.question: Has the contamination risk from other materials touching the equipment or product been considered (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the risk of contamination from other materials that come into direct contact with manufacturing equipment or the product (such as media used for process simulation tests and lubricants that may contact the product) is also taken into account (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing how this contamination risk was taken into account

points.question: For allogeneic products that need no donor-patient match, is a master and working seed lot/cell bank system in use (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the system of master and working seed lots/cell banks is used for allogeneic products which do not require a match between the donor and the patient (recommended).

evidence.what: seed lot / cell bank system description
master and working seed lot / cell bank records

points.question: Where seed lots and cell banks are used, do records show they were set up under suitable, GMP-compliant conditions in a controlled environment (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, when seed lots and cell banks, including master and working generations, are used, they are established under appropriate conditions, including compliance with GMP as provided for in these Guidelines (recommended). Verify that this includes an appropriately controlled environment to protect the seed lot and the cell bank and the personnel handling it (recommended).

evidence.what: seed lot / cell bank establishment records
environment where seed lots / cell banks are established

points.question: While a seed lot or cell bank is being set up, is the area kept free of work with any other living or infectious material (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, during the establishment of the seed lot and cell bank, no other living or infectious material (e.g. virus, cell lines or cell strains) is handled simultaneously in the same area (recommended).

evidence.what: area use records during seed lot / cell bank establishment
area during seed lot / cell bank establishment

points.question: Do records show that the number of generations matches what the authorisation specifies (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the number of generations (doublings, passages) is consistent with specifications in the marketing authorisation/clinical trial authorisation (recommended).

evidence.what: marketing authorisation / clinical trial authorisation specifications
records of generations (doublings, passages)

points.question: Is there documentation that supports traceability for the stages before the master seed or cell bank was generated (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, for stages prior to the master seed or cell bank generation, documentation is available to support traceability, including issues related to components used during development with potential impact on product safety (e.g. reagents of biological origin), from initial sourcing and genetic development if applicable (recommended).

evidence.what: traceability documentation for stages before master seed / cell bank

points.question: Are starting materials from old seed lots/cell banks with incomplete information used only exceptionally and backed by extensive characterisation?

points.question: Is the QC laboratory apart from the production area?

points.question: Where supplier certificates replace testing of starting materials, are the three conditions for this met (recommended)?

points.question: Are enough samples of intermediate and final products kept, stored suitably and for a suitable time?

points.question: Is there a written protocol that sets out the sampling procedure?

points.question: Is the quality assurance programme put into practice and followed?

points.question: Does each reference standard have a quality that suits what it is used for?

points.question: For a phytopharmaceutical not in a recognised pharmacopoeia, is a herbarium sample on hand?

points.question: Are reference standards kept in conditions that stop them degrading?

points.question: Are plant preparation specifications made up of the relevant plant material or finished product specification items?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications of plant preparations consist, depending on the preparation in question, of the relevant items of the specifications for plant materials or for finished phytopharmaceutical products as specified in the preceding paragraph [Part VI 18.1 and 19].

points.question: Do the specifications concentrate on the characteristics that help ensure safety and efficacy?

points.question: Is a reference sample on hand for identifying the plant material?

points.question: Do starting material and packaging material specifications refer to a pharmacopoeial monograph where one applies?

primary and printed packaging material specifications

points.question: Do the specifications state the norms for rejecting, storing and disposing of plant material that fails?

points.question: Is information on the active ingredients of plant materials and preparations given in the described way?

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, name the plant family and the full botanical name?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for plant materials as far as possible include, as a minimum, the family and botanical name of the plant used according to the binomial system (genus, species, variety and the authority, i.e., the reference to the originator of the classification, e.g., Linnaeus).

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, give the details of where and how the plant was sourced?

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, say what part of the plant is used and its state, and the drying system if applicable?

evidence.what: plant material specifications

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, describe the material as seen by eye, under the microscope or both?

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, contain suitable identity tests, with identification tests where appropriate?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for plant materials as far as possible include, as a minimum, suitable identity tests including, where appropriate, identification tests (such as Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) or other chromatographic fingerprint) for known active ingredients or markers.

evidence.what: plant material specifications

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, give assay details for active constituents or markers where appropriate?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for plant materials as far as possible include, as a minimum, details of the assay, where appropriate, of active constituents or markers.

evidence.what: plant material specifications

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, contain limit tests?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for plant materials as far as possible include, as a minimum, limit tests such as dry residue of liquids, ash value (total ash and ash insoluble in hydrochloric acid), water-soluble extractives, moisture or water content and loss on drying (taking into account the presence of essential oils if any).

evidence.what: plant material specifications

points.question: Do the specifications, as far as possible, give methods and acceptable limits for pesticide contamination?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for plant materials as far as possible include, as a minimum, suitable methods for the determination of possible pesticide contamination and the acceptable limits for such contamination in plant materials or plant preparations used in the manufacture of Phytopharmaceuticals.

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, contain tests for toxic metals, contaminants, foreign matter and adulterants?

evidence.what: plant material specifications

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, contain tests and limits for fungal, microbial and similar contamination?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for plant materials as far as possible include, as a minimum, tests for fungal, microbiological contamination, fumigant residues (if applicable), mycotoxins (aflatoxins), pest-infestations, radioactivity and their acceptable limits.

evidence.what: plant material specifications

points.question: Do plant material specifications, as far as possible, contain other appropriate tests?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for plant materials as far as possible include, as a minimum, other appropriate tests (e.g., particle size, swelling index and residual solvents in Phytopharmaceutical preparations and biological fingerprints such as induced fluorescent markers).

evidence.what: plant material specifications

points.question: Do finished product specifications contain tests for microbial contamination and other toxicants?

points.question: Do finished product specifications contain the dosage-form tests that apply?

evidence.what: finished phytopharmaceutical specifications

points.question: Do finished product specifications cover physical appearance and loss on drying or water content?

points.question: Do finished product specifications contain identity tests for the plant substances?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for finished phytopharmaceuticals include identity tests, qualitative determination of relevant substances of the plants (e.g., fingerprint chromatograms).

evidence.what: finished phytopharmaceutical specifications

points.question: Do finished product specifications cover how much of the identified active ingredients is present and the methods for this?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for finished phytopharmaceuticals include quantification of relevant active ingredients, if they have been identified, and the analytical methods that are available.

evidence.what: finished phytopharmaceutical specifications

points.question: Do finished product specifications contain residual solvent limit tests?
points.verify: Verify that the specifications for finished phytopharmaceuticals include limit tests for residual solvents.

evidence.what: finished phytopharmaceutical specifications

points.question: Do finished product specifications follow the Indian Pharmacopoeia general monograph for the dosage form?

points.question: Can the main active constituents of the finished product be identified and measured with the set tests and specifications?

points.question: Are active constituents or markers named in the documents, and are assay specifications set for them?
points.verify: Verify that, if the therapeutic activity of constituents is known, these constituents are indicated in the documentation; that, if such substances are not known (e.g., because they are part of a complex mixture), the constituents useful for assessing the quality are identified as markers; and that in both cases the assay (i.e., quantitative determination) specifications are defined.

points.question: Where a mixture of active ingredients is determined instead of each one, is the need for this justified?

points.question: Have adequate retest periods been set for plant materials and plant preparations?

points.question: Do QC staff know phytopharmaceuticals well enough to identify materials and spot problems in a consignment?

points.question: Does quality control establish the quality of plant materials, preparations and finished plant products?

points.question: Is plant material sampled with special care by people who have the needed expertise?

points.question: Are identification methods specific, and ideally able to tell the right plant material from likely substitutes or adulterants?

points.question: For groups (a) and (b), can the identification methods detect the active ingredients, and does the label state at least the main ones?

points.question: Are test animals kept and controlled so that they stay suitable for their intended use (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that animals used for testing are maintained and controlled in a manner that assures their suitability for the intended use (recommended).

evidence.what: maintenance and control of test animals
records showing how test animals are maintained and controlled

points.question: Are test animals identified, and do adequate records show how each has been used (recommended)?

evidence.what: identification of test animals
records of the history of use of test animals

points.question: Where official compendial reference standards exist, are these preferably used as the primary standards unless there is full justification (recommended)?

evidence.what: records of reference standards in use
justification, and traceability documents for secondary standards

points.question: Are compendial materials used only for the monograph purpose, unless the National Competent Authority has authorised otherwise (recommended)?

evidence.what: records of use of compendial reference standards
authorisation by the National Competent Authority, if any

points.question: Is product stability followed after marketing under a continuous programme able to pick up stability problems (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, after marketing, the stability of the medicinal product is monitored according to a continuous appropriate programme that will permit the detection of any stability issue (e.g. changes in levels of impurities or dissolution profile) associated with the formulation in the marketed package (recommended).

evidence.what: on-going stability programme
on-going stability data

points.question: Has the site considered adding bulk product to the on-going stability programme (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, while the programme mainly applies to the medicinal product in the package in which it is sold, consideration is also given to the inclusion in the programme of bulk product (recommended).

evidence.what: programme or records showing this consideration

references.rule: joined item: unit inside sub-clause EU C6 6.27

points.question: When bulk product waits a long time before packing or shipment to a packaging site, is the effect on packaged product stability assessed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, for example, when the bulk product is stored for a long period before being packaged and/or shipped from a manufacturing site to a packaging site, the impact on the stability of the packaged product is evaluated and studied under ambient conditions (recommended).

evidence.what: evaluation and study records of this impact

references.rule: joined item: unit inside sub-clause EU C6 6.28

points.question: Has the site considered intermediates that are stored and used over long periods (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in addition, consideration is given to intermediates that are stored and used over prolonged periods (recommended).

evidence.what: programme or records showing this consideration

references.rule: joined item: unit inside sub-clause EU C6 6.28

points.question: Is the on-going stability programme set out in a written protocol, with results issued as a report (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the on-going stability programme is described in a written protocol following the general rules of Chapter 4 and that results are formalised as a report (recommended).

evidence.what: on-going stability protocol
on-going stability report

points.question: Is the equipment used for on-going stability, such as stability chambers, qualified and maintained (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the equipment used for the on-going stability programme (stability chambers among others) is qualified and maintained following the general rules of Chapter 3 and Annex 15 (recommended).

evidence.what: qualification records of the equipment
maintenance records of the equipment

points.question: Does the on-going stability protocol run to the end of shelf life and cover at least all the listed parameters (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the protocol for an on-going stability programme extends to the end of the shelf life period and includes, but is not limited to: number of batch(es) per strength and different batch sizes, if applicable; relevant physical, chemical, microbiological and biological test methods; acceptance criteria; reference to test methods; description of the container closure system(s); testing intervals (time points); description of the conditions of storage (standardised ICH/VICH conditions for long term testing, consistent with the product labelling, are used); and other applicable parameters specific to the medicinal product (recommended).

evidence.what: on-going stability protocol

points.question: Where the on-going stability protocol differs from the initial long-term study in the marketing authorisation dossier, is the difference justified and documented in the protocol (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the protocol for the on-going stability programme is different from that of the initial long-term stability study as submitted in the marketing authorisation dossier (for example the frequency of testing, or when updating to ICH/VICH recommendations), this is justified and documented in the protocol (recommended).

evidence.what: on-going stability protocol

points.question: Do the batch numbers and testing frequency give enough data for trend analysis (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the number of batches and frequency of testing provide a sufficient amount of data to allow for trend analysis (recommended).

evidence.what: on-going stability protocol
on-going stability data

points.question: Does the stability programme take in at least one batch a year for each strength and primary pack type, unless justified (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, unless otherwise justified, at least one batch per year of product manufactured in every strength and every primary packaging type, if relevant, is included in the stability programme (unless none are produced during that year) (recommended).

evidence.what: records of batches included in the stability programme
justification, if any

points.question: Where bracketing and matrixing designs are used, is this scientifically justified in the protocol (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where the principle of bracketing and matrixing designs is applied, it is scientifically justified in the protocol (recommended).

evidence.what: on-going stability protocol

points.question: Are extra batches put on on-going stability in certain situations, for example after a significant change or deviation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in certain situations, additional batches are included in the on-going stability programme; for example, that an on-going stability study is conducted after any significant change or significant deviation to the process or package (recommended).

evidence.what: records of batches included in the on-going stability programme

points.question: Is each reworking, reprocessing or recovery operation considered for adding to the stability programme (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that any reworking, reprocessing or recovery operation is also considered for inclusion in the on-going stability programme (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing this consideration

points.question: Do key staff, especially the Qualified Person(s), get the on-going stability results (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that results of on-going stability studies are made available to key personnel and, in particular, to the Qualified Person(s) (recommended).

evidence.what: records showing results made available
key personnel and Qualified Person(s)

points.question: Where on-going stability studies are done at another site, is there a written agreement between the parties (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, where on-going stability studies are carried out at a site other than the site of manufacture of the bulk or finished product, there is a written agreement between the parties concerned (recommended).

evidence.what: written agreement between the parties

points.question: Can the manufacturing site show on-going stability results to the competent authority for review (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that results of on-going stability studies are available at the site of manufacture for review by the competent authority (recommended).

evidence.what: on-going stability results held at the site of manufacture

points.question: Are out of specification results or significant atypical trends in stability investigated (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that out of specification or significant atypical trends are investigated (recommended).

points.question: Are confirmed out of specification results or significant negative trends that affect marketed batches reported to the authorities (recommended)?

points.question: Is the possible effect on batches already on the market assessed, together with the authorities (recommended)?

points.question: Is a summary of all stability data, with any interim conclusions, written, kept and reviewed periodically (recommended)?

records of periodic review of the summary

points.question: Before a method transfer, does the sending site confirm that the method matches the Marketing Authorisation or technical dossier (recommended)?

points.question: Is the original method validation reviewed against current ICH/VICH requirements (recommended)?

points.question: Is a documented gap analysis done before the transfer starts, to find any extra validation needed (recommended)?

points.question: Does the transfer protocol cover at least all the listed parameters (recommended)?

points.question: Are protocol deviations investigated before the technical transfer is closed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that deviations from the protocol are investigated prior to closure of the technical transfer process (recommended).

points.question: Does the transfer report record the comparative outcome and name any areas needing more revalidation (recommended)?

points.question: Where appropriate, are specific requirements of other European Guidelines dealt with when particular methods are transferred (recommended)?

technical transfer report

points.question: Is each batch of material given at least one identity test, apart from the excepted materials (recommended)?

points.question: Where a supplier's Certificate of Analysis replaces other tests, does the manufacturer have a supplier evaluation system (recommended)?

points.question: Are the specifications, sampling plans and test methods soundly based and fit to show that materials meet the set quality standards (recommended)?

sampling plans
test procedures

registration/filing

records of changes to these documents

points.question: Are laboratory controls carried out as laid down and written up when the work is done (recommended)?

laboratory work and how it is recorded

out-of-specification investigation records

points.question: Does the out-of-specification procedure call for data analysis, a judgement on whether there is a significant problem, assigned corrective action tasks and conclusions (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that the out-of-specification procedure calls for analysis of the data, assessment of whether a significant problem exists, allocation of the tasks for corrective actions, and conclusions (recommended).

records of re-sampling and retesting after OOS results

points.question: Is there normally an impurity profile for each API (recommended)?

points.question: Does the Certificate of Analysis give the product name, grade where appropriate, batch number and release date (recommended)?

points.question: Where an intermediate or API has an expiry date, is that date on both the label and the Certificate of Analysis (recommended)?

labels of intermediates or APIs

points.question: Where an intermediate or API has a retest date, is that date shown on the label and/or the Certificate of Analysis (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that for intermediates or APIs with a retest date, the retest date is indicated on the label and/or Certificate of Analysis (recommended).

labels of intermediates or APIs

points.question: Do new certificates issued by or for repackers/reprocessors, agents or brokers give the contact details of the testing laboratory (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that if new Certificates are issued by or on behalf of repackers/reprocessors, agents or brokers, these Certificates show the name, address and telephone number of the laboratory that performed the analysis (recommended).

evidence.what: new Certificates issued by or on behalf of repackers/reprocessors, agents or brokers

points.question: Do such new certificates refer to the original manufacturer and the original batch certificate, with a copy of it attached (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that these new Certificates also contain a reference to the name and address of the original manufacturer and to the original batch Certificate, and that a copy of the original batch Certificate is attached (recommended).

points.question: Are APIs with short shelf-lives put through stability testing more often (recommended)?

stability test records

points.question: For APIs with a shelf-life of one year or less, are stability samples taken and tested monthly for three months and then every three months (recommended)?

stability sample and test records

stability storage condition records

description of stability sample containers and market container

points.question: Were the first three commercial batches normally put on stability monitoring to confirm the retest or expiry date (recommended)?

points.question: Where fewer than three batches were put on stability, do earlier study data show the API is expected to stay stable for at least two years (recommended)?

points.question: After the first batches, is at least one API batch a year added to stability monitoring and tested at least yearly (recommended)?

points.question: Where a stability test interval has been dropped, is this backed by data confirming the API's stability is not compromised (recommended)?
points.verify: Where elimination of specific test intervals (e.g. 9 month testing) is used, verify that data exist that confirm that the stability of the API is not compromised (recommended).

evidence.what: stability data supporting the dropped test intervals

points.question: Where release tests on the active substance or finished product cannot be done, has an adequate control strategy been designed (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that, in cases where it is not possible to perform the release tests on the active substance or the finished product, an adequate control strategy has been designed (recommended).

evidence.what: control strategy

points.question: Where key intermediates or in-process controls are tested in place of finished product or batch release testing, can the relevance of the results be shown (recommended)?
points.verify: Where testing of key intermediates (instead of the finished product) or in-process controls (instead of batch release testing) is used, verify that the relevance of the results from these tests to the critical quality attributes of the finished product can be demonstrated (recommended).

data showing relevance of the results to the critical quality attributes

points.question: Where scarce material or a very short shelf-life limits release controls, is this made up for by stronger process validation (recommended)?
points.verify: Verify that when the scarcity of materials or the very short shelf-life limits the possibilities for release controls, the limitations are compensated by a reinforced process validation (e.g. additional assays, such as potency testing or proliferation assays, may be performed after batch release as supporting data for process validation) (recommended).

process validation data

points.question: Does release testing follow the marketing or clinical trial authorisation (recommended)?

release test records

points.question: Where the pharmacopoeial sterility test on the finished product cannot be done or awaited before release, has the sterility assurance strategy been adapted?

points.question: Where alternative rapid microbiological methods are used, are they validated (recommended)?

points.question: When sterility test results are not there at release, are suitable mitigation steps taken, including telling the treating physician (recommended)?

records of informing the treating physician

points.question: Where an appearance test replaces the particulate matter test for cells in suspension, are alternative measures in place (recommended)?

points.question: Is there enough suitable space to store samples and records (recommended)?

points.question: Are the quality control laboratories normally kept apart from production areas (recommended)?

site layout

person responsible for quality control

points.question: Where in-process controls are done inside the production area, are they free of any risk for the product (recommended)?
points.verify: Where in-process controls are carried out within the production area, verify that they do not carry any risk for the product (recommended).
